# Exact label-information retention of arbitrary quantum preparations

30 October 2026, Brisbane. Root's central construction, developed with C's
pure-frame extraction and B's independent modular reconstruction. Independent
whole-file challenge is pending. This is a supplied finite-channel theorem,
not physical channel acquisition or historical-priority clearance.

## 1. Operation and exact statement

Let n>=2 and let tau_1,...,tau_n be finite-dimensional density matrices.
The input label X is EXPLICITLY classical. The preparation channel sends
i to tau_i. For arbitrary finite quantum reference R and classical-quantum
hypotheses rho_XR,sigma_XR, define

 J_X=D(rho_XR||sigma_XR)-D(rho_R||sigma_R),
 J_tau=D((tau tensor id)rho||(tau tensor id)sigma)-D(rho_R||sigma_R).

Only defined finite differences are admitted. Let S be the support of
sum_j tau_j and let Pi_i project, WITHIN S, onto the kernel of
sum_(j!=i)tau_j. Set r_i=Tr(tau_i Pi_i), r=min_i r_i.

**Theorem.** For every admitted pair and every finite R,

    J_tau >= r J_X.                                      (1)

The constant r is SHARP, even restricting R to dimension1 and using
equal-reference hypotheses. Thus the sharp reverse factor is1/r if r>0,
and infinite if r=0. Equivalently,

 D_out >= r D_in+(1-r)D_reference.                        (2)

This does NOT follow merely from D_out>=rD_in. No classical-output
equal-reference/conditional equivalence is imported for these quantum
outputs. The changing-reference term is proved below.

For rational density matrices, kernel projectors, r_i and the sharp factor
are acquired by polynomial exact rational linear algebra. No optimization
over reference states, matrix logarithm or eigenvalue precision oracle is
needed for this operation. Exact supports are substantive input information.

## 2. The algebraic extraction identity

Assume first every r_i>0, and put E_i=Pi_i/r_i. On output Hilbert--Schmidt
space define T(Y)_i=Tr(E_iY), with adjoint T*e_i=E_i. This linear extraction
is NOT claimed to be a jointly normalized POVM.

Positivity implies Pi_i tau_j=tau_j Pi_i=0 for j!=i. Therefore

 T|tau_j>=e_j,
 T L_tau_j T*=T R_tau_j T*=(1/r_j)|j><j|.                 (3)

For example the (i,k) entry of the first identity of operators is
Tr(E_i tau_j E_k): it vanishes unless i=k=j, when it equals
Tr(tau_j Pi_j)/r_j^2=1/r_j. The right-multiplication case follows by
cyclicity of trace with the SAME complex cross terms. The Pi_i need not
be mutually orthogonal. This is precisely why replacing T by an unambiguous
measurement's simultaneous normalization would lose the sharp constant.

For ANY two positive operator families X_i^L,X_i^R on an auxiliary space,
let Q_i=X_i^L+X_i^R and

 W=sum_i L_tau_i tensor X_i^L+R_tau_i tensor X_i^R,
 v=sum_i |tau_i> tensor u_i.

Equation(3) gives

 (T tensor I)W(T* tensor I)=diag(Q_i/r_i),
 (T tensor I)v=col(u_i).

The inverse-form Cauchy inequality, or the variational formula for
v*W^-1v, consequently proves

    <v,W^-1v> >= sum_i r_i<u_i,Q_i^-1u_i>.               (4)

Use faithful weights/restrict to S where necessary; actual modular weights
below are positive. No unsupported one-family CQ Fisher equality is used.

## 3. A direct unequal-reference modular gauge

Take faithful input blocks A_i>0 and Hermitian tangent blocks H_i. Write
M=sum_i A_i, H=sum_i H_i. For s in(0,1), on reference Hilbert--Schmidt
space put

 Q_i=s L_Ai+(1-s)R_Ai, Z=sum_i Q_i,
 z=Z^-1 H, u_i=H_i-Q_i z.

Then sum_i u_i=0 and square completion gives the input conditional
modular Hessian

 sum_i <H_i,Q_i^-1 H_i>-<H,Z^-1H>
      =sum_i <u_i,Q_i^-1u_i>.                           (5)

The output modular operator on HS(S) tensor HS(R) is

 W=s sum_i L_tau_i tensor L_Ai
           +(1-s)sum_i R_tau_i tensor R_Ai.

Its tangent is v_H=sum_i|tau_i> tensor H_i. Because Tr(tau_i)=1,

 W(|I_S> tensor z)=sum_i|tau_i> tensor Q_i z,
 <I_S tensor z,W(I_S tensor z)>=<z,Zz>.

The cross term of v_u=sum_i|tau_i> tensor u_i with I_S tensor z
vanishes by sum_i u_i=0. Thus the output conditional modular Hessian is
EXACTLY

    <v_H,W^-1v_H>-<H,Z^-1H>=<v_u,W^-1v_u>.              (6)

Apply(4) with X_i^L=s L_Ai and X_i^R=(1-s)R_Ai. Equations(5),(6) give
the conditional modular comparison with factor r for EVERY s. Integrate
over s using the ordinary BKM divided-difference representation
g_A(H)=integral_0^1 <H,[sL_A+(1-s)R_A]^-1H> ds.
Then integrate the Hessian along the affine path from sigma to rho with
Taylor weight1-t. The Bregman differences are exactly J_tau and J_X.
This proves(1),(2) for faithful hypotheses with arbitrary reference change.

Finite-divergence boundary hypotheses follow by mixing BOTH with the SAME
faithful cq state on the common input/reference support and passing to the
common-mixture limit. Output space is restricted to S, on which faithful
input blocks give faithful outputs. Infinite-minus-infinite is never used.
If r=0, inequality(1) is simply conditional DPI/nonnegativity; sharpness
is still established next.

## 4. Sharpness with ordinary classical endpoint priors

Fix i. Choose positive weights w_j for j!=i summing to1 and let
omega=sum_(j!=i)w_j tau_j. Compare input rho=|i><i| with the faithful
prior q_i=epsilon, q_j=(1-epsilon)w_j. Their classical divergence is
log(1/epsilon). The output comparison is tau_i versus

    Omega_epsilon=(1-epsilon)omega+epsilon tau_i.

Inside S, Pi_i is exactly ker omega. The compression Pi_i tau_i Pi_i
is positive definite on this kernel: a vector killed by both omega and
tau_i would lie outside S. Small eigenvalues of Omega_epsilon are therefore
Theta(epsilon), with cluster projector Pi_i+O(epsilon); remaining eigenvalues
are bounded away from0. Equivalently, min-max plus
Omega_epsilon>=epsilon(omega+tau_i) for epsilon<=1/2 and the fixed positive
gap of omega on its range gives

    log Omega_epsilon=(log epsilon)Pi_i+O(1).

The cluster-projector error times log epsilon remains bounded. Hence

 D(tau_i||Omega_epsilon)=r_i log(1/epsilon)+O(1).          (7)

The ratio tends to r_i. If Pi_i=0 the output divergence stays bounded,
so the ratio tends to0. These hypotheses have trivial/equal reference;
if faithful rho is desired, regularize it on a smaller scale and use
continuity at each positive epsilon. Equation(7) proves sharpness and
the zero convention without a quantum-reference search or a claimed
favorable rate uniform over channels.

## 5. An explicit finite Choi certificate

The inequality also has a direct coefficient certificate for the two-family
source pencil diag(X_i^L,X_i^R) direct_sum [[W,V],[V*,I]], where
V=sum_i|tau_i> tensor U_i and sum_i U_i=0. The classical-label target is
[[diag(Q_i),U],[U*,cI]], with c=1/r=max_i1/r_i.

Use the arrow Kraus Z/sqrt(c), where Z's upper block is T* and its bottom
entry is c. Its congruence gives target top diag(Q_i/(c r_i)), exact U
offdiagonal and bottom cI. Fill each diagonal deficit
(1-1/(c r_i))Q_i from BOTH corresponding source effect blocks. All fills
are nonnegative. Under the source-first convention
C_(a,p),(b,q)=[Phi(E_ab)]_(p,q), Phi(A)=Z* A Z/c has rank-one Choi matrix
vec(conjugate Z) vec(conjugate Z)*/c, with (a,p) source/output ordering.
These rational outer products and the scalar diagonal fills require no
evaluated square root. Using ZZ* here would have the wrong dimension;
the vectorization/conjugation is essential for complex preparations.
This is a solver-free CP pencil certificate, not a physical degrader.
C independently executed the SAME binary0,+ case's27-order rank1 Choi
coefficient identity in c_cq_extension/EXACT_TWO_FAMILY.json.

## 6. Acquisition, predecessors and limits

Kernel projectors of rational Hermitian matrices are rational: for any
rational full-column kernel basis V use V(V*V)^-1V*. One may compute the
kernel of sum_(j!=i)tau_j in the full output space; the common kernel of
all tau_j contributes zero to r_i and can be subtracted as a nested
projector. Exact rank/linear algebra and traces have polynomial bit cost.
No arbitrary numerical near-zero eigenvalue is declared an exact support.

For independent pure preparations with Gram G, r_i=1/(G^-1)_ii. The sharp
reverse factor is max_i(G^-1)_ii. For |0>,|+>, r=1/2 and it is2. The
ordinary heralded inverse has uniform success1-1/sqrt2, a different physical
operation with weaker bound2+sqrt2. UDM reciprocal states/support subspaces
are established predecessors (Rudolph--Spekkens--Turner2003; Chefles1998),
not new inventions here. B's general pure-pair resolvent proof independently
earns the equal-reference answer; this proof pays the full conditional and
mixed-output operation. Precise broader-world priority remains UNKNOWN.

The exact coefficient is NOT robust under unrestricted channel uncertainty:
any positive full-rank contamination of every preparation makes r=0 for
n>=2. This is a material access boundary, not a physically stable inverse.
The theorem concerns supplied state matrices and a worst-case information
ratio. It does not acquire a quantum experiment, jointly normalized UDM,
capacity, guessing/privacy order, a correlated-block constant or a
civilisation-level operational technology. Product-source retention is
multiplicative at the full product alphabet, as independently derived by B;
it does not make the same single-use reverse factor unchanged under reuse.

## 7. A finite rational witness for a rejected reverse factor

B independently supplied a constructive endpoint bound in
b_mixed_retention_challenge/FINITE_WITNESS.md; root reconstructs the bound
and accepts it at the scope below. This is a separate contributor extension,
not an independently audited numerical entropy-state experiment.

For a proposed finite reverse factor c with c r_i<1, form the rational
uniform mixture omega of all other preparations and P=ker omega within S.
Acquire rational floors 0<a,b<=1 for the positive eigenvalues of
tau_i+omega on S and omega on its range. Rational pseudoinverse traces
give such floors without an orthonormal-basis or spectral oracle. In full
space, A^+=(A+Pker(A))^-1-Pker(A), all rational.

For epsilon<=ab/8, omega_epsilon>=
(epsilon a/2)P+(b/4)(I-P). Operator monotonicity of log and
Tr(tau_i log tau_i)<=0 therefore give the conservative finite bound

    D(tau_i||omega_epsilon)
       <=r_i log(1/epsilon)+log(8/(ab)).

One may see the matrix lower bound directly by writing
omega_epsilon=epsilon(tau_i+omega)+(1-2epsilon)omega and using the two
acquired floors; no unjustified eigenvector alignment is required.
Choose integer h with2^h>=8/(ab), then an integer k>=h with
k>c h/(1-c r_i). The rational priors p=e_i and
q_i=2^-k,q_j=(1-2^-k)/(n-1) give STRICT

    D_input=k log2 > c D_output.

Thus the returned finite pair certifies rejection without evaluating any
logarithm. It has trivial reference, finite divergences and a faithful q;
p is a permitted boundary input. If r_i=0 the same operation works for
every finite c. The bit length k of this explicit witness may be large
in the gap1-c r_i and conditioning. Polynomial acquisition of the sharp
coefficient is not a polynomial short-witness claim in their logarithms.

# Independent mixed-retention reconstruction

Derived from the supplied claim before the producer's full proof existed on
disk. This is an analytic reconstruction, not yet a whole-file intake.

## Exact mathematical claim

Take `n>=2` density matrices `tau_i` on a finite output space. Restrict the
output to `S=supp(sum_i tau_i)`. Within S define

`P_i=projector ker(sum_(j!=i) tau_j)`, `r_i=Tr tau_i P_i`, `r=min_i r_i`.

The proposed complete conditional minimum retention is r. In particular,
for every finite reference and every cq state pair with the relevant
relative entropies finite,

`D(T rho||T sigma)-D(rho_R||sigma_R)
 >= r [D(rho||sigma)-D(rho_R||sigma_R)]`.               (A)

For r>0 its reverse coefficient is exactly1/r; for r=0 no finite reverse
coefficient works. The same r is the minimum retention without subtraction
and on the equal-reference restriction. Sharpness needs no reference.

The requirement n>=2 is necessary for the sharp *conditional* coefficient
statement: at n=1 both conditional quantities vanish identically. This
does not affect ordinary all-D retention, where the singleton channel is
the identity on the reference and has coefficient1.

## 1. The Hilbert--Schmidt extraction is exact but is not a POVM

For r_i>0 set `E_i=P_i/r_i` and define the linear map from output HS space
to C^n by `(T X)_i=Tr E_i X`. With the complex Hilbert--Schmidt product,

`T* z=sum_i z_i E_i`, `T(tau_j)=e_j`.

There is no extra conjugate in the first formula: E_i is Hermitian and
the inner product is conjugate-linear in its first argument. If k!=j,
both `E_k tau_j=0` and `tau_j E_k=0`. Hence

`(T L_tau_j T*)_(kl)=Tr E_k tau_j E_l
                   =delta_kj delta_lj/r_j`,
`(T R_tau_j T*)_(kl)=Tr E_k E_l tau_j
                   =delta_kj delta_lj/r_j`.           (B)

For k=l=j the equality uses P_j^2=P_j and cyclicity, not commutativity
of P_j with tau_j. For every other pair, one of the annihilation
identities kills the term. Thus all complex cross terms are paid.

For arbitrary positive reference-HS operators Q_i^L,Q_i^R, let

`W=sum_i [L_tau_i tensor Q_i^L + R_tau_i tensor Q_i^R]`,
`Q_i=Q_i^L+Q_i^R`, `y=sum_i tau_i tensor u_i`.

Then (B) implies

`(T tensor I) W(T* tensor I)=diag(Q_i/r_i)`,
`(T tensor I)y=(u_i)_i`.

For W>0, the elementary inverse-form projection inequality gives

`<y,W^-1 y> >= sum_i r_i <u_i,Q_i^-1 u_i>`.            (C)

One self-contained proof is to subtract the right side: it equals
`||W^-1/2 y-W^1/2 T*(TWT*)^-1 Ty||^2`.
The same statement on finite inverse-form domains follows by adding a
positive regulator. For physical faithful blocks below, W is already
positive on the restricted S output, so no boundary inverse is needed.

The extraction is not asserted to be trace-preserving or even a
measurement: the E_i need not sum below identity. Thus (C) is an
information inequality, not a simultaneous label-recovery probability.

## 2. Full unequal-reference modular gauge

Let the faithful cq baseline be `diag(A_i)` with A_i>0, and let H_i be
Hermitian tangent blocks. For each v in[0,1], on the reference HS space put

`Q_i=(1-v)L_Ai+v R_Ai`, `Q=sum_i Q_i`,
`h=sum_i H_i`, `z=Q^-1 h`, `u_i=H_i-Q_i z`.

Then `sum_i u_i=0`, and completing the square gives EXACTLY

`sum_i <H_i,Q_i^-1 H_i>-<h,Q^-1 h>
    =sum_i <u_i,Q_i^-1 u_i>`.                         (D)

On output HS tensor reference HS use

`W=(1-v)L_(sum tau_i tensor A_i)+v R_(sum tau_i tensor A_i)`,
`Y=sum_i tau_i tensor H_i`, `U=sum_i tau_i tensor u_i`.

Here `W(I_S tensor z)=sum_i tau_i tensor Q_i z`. The cross term in
the output completion vanishes because Tr tau_i=1 and sum_i u_i=0.
The constant term is <h,Q^-1 h>, again exactly. Therefore

`<Y,W^-1Y>-<h,Q^-1h>=<U,W^-1U>`.

Applying (C), then r_i>=r, proves the conditional inequality at every
modular parameter v. Integration of

`Dlog(A)=integral_0^1 [(1-v)L_A+vR_A]^-1 dv`

proves the conditional BKM inequality. Integrate that Hessian along the
state line sigma+t(rho-sigma), with weight1-t, to obtain (A). The
reference entropy is the Hessian of the SAME reference state line, so
this argument never imports an equal-reference/classical-output theorem.

All these HS spaces are complex. The normalizing z may be non-Hermitian
at v!=1/2; it is used only inside a complex positive quadratic form.
There is no requirement that the intermediate u_i represent a physical
Hermitian tangent. The actual H_i do represent that tangent; C permits
arbitrary complex u_i, which is exactly what closes the gauge.

Finite defined boundary differences follow by common faithful
regularization. Each finite D converges individually by joint convexity
and lower semicontinuity. Undefined infinity-minus-infinity is excluded.

## 3. Endpoint sharpness, including noncommuting mixed outputs

Fix label i. Let `B=sum_(j!=i) w_j tau_j`, where all w_j>0 and sum w_j=1,
and take the scalar input hypotheses `p=e_i`,
`q_e=e e_i+(1-e)sum_(j!=i)w_j e_j`. The input divergence is log(1/e).
The output second state is `B_e=(1-e)B+e tau_i`.

In the restricted total output S, split off ker B. Let
`a=lambda_min(B+tau_i)>0` and let b>0 be the least positive eigenvalue
of B. For e<=1/2, `B_e>=e(B+tau_i)>=e a I`. On ker B, its Rayleigh
quotient is at most `e||tau_i||<=e`. The min--max principle thus traps
each of the dim(ker B) small eigenvalues between e a and e; the other
eigenvalues stay at least b/2. Separated spectral perturbation gives
`||P_small(e)-P_i||=O(e/b)`. Therefore:

* all small nonzero eigenvalues of B_e are e times fixed positive
  quantities, bounded above and below by constants times e;
* their joint spectral projector converges to P_i with error O(e);
* the other eigenvalues stay bounded below.

Thus

`D(tau_i||B_e)=r_i log(1/e)+O(1)`                     (E)

(an O(e log(1/e)) projector correction is bounded). If r_i=0, tau_i is
supported inside supp B and the output divergence stays finite. Hence
the minimum retained fraction is at most every r_i, and is exactly r by
(A). All e>0 divergences here are finite. Perturbing p into the strict
simplex interior at each fixed e preserves the same limiting supremum.

## 4. Exact acquisition versus fragile physical admission

For exactly supplied rational complex Hermitian preparations, each P_i
and r_i is rational and can be computed without eigenvalue/logarithm
oracles. Obtain a rational full-column-rank basis Z_i of the kernel of
`sum_(j!=i)tau_j` by Gaussian elimination, then

`P_i=Z_i(Z_i*Z_i)^-1 Z_i*`, `r_i=Tr tau_i P_i`.

All Gaussian elimination, inversion and exact comparison steps have
polynomial rational bit cost in the explicit matrix input size. Zero
kernel gives P_i=0 and r_i=0. A producer routine must check Hermiticity,
normalization and positive semidefiniteness or declare those as input
promises; it cannot infer them from decimal tolerances.

This is not a robust finite-precision physical inverse. For n>=2, replace
each preparation by `(1-delta)tau_i+delta I/d` for ANY delta>0. Every
preparation is faithful, so P_i=0 for all i and the universal reverse
coefficient is infinite. Arbitrarily small unrestricted channel error
therefore changes a finite coefficient to infinity. Exact support
structure is a real admission gate. Bounded-away-from-boundary priors
would be a different problem, not the theorem being challenged.

When all r_i>0, one can choose a vector from each private functional
space that separates its label. This implies n<=d; in fact
rank(tau_i)<=d-n+1. Consequently the finite-coefficient case has
substantial rank-deficient geometry, already familiar from unambiguous
discrimination. It is not a generic full-rank cq channel property.

## 5. Optional structural consequence: product sources

For product preparations indexed by(i,j), the span of all OTHER labels is

`[span_(k!=i)supp(tau_k)] tensor S_B
 +S_A tensor [span_(l!=j)supp(omega_l)]`.

Its orthogonal complement is the tensor product of the two private

# Exact label-information retention of arbitrary quantum preparations

30 October 2026, Brisbane. Root's central construction, developed with C's
pure-frame extraction and B's independent modular reconstruction. Independent
whole-file challenge is pending. This is a supplied finite-channel theorem,
not physical channel acquisition or historical-priority clearance.

## 1. Operation and exact statement

Let n>=2 and let tau_1,...,tau_n be finite-dimensional density matrices.
The input label X is EXPLICITLY classical. The preparation channel sends
i to tau_i. For arbitrary finite quantum reference R and classical-quantum
hypotheses rho_XR,sigma_XR, define

 J_X=D(rho_XR||sigma_XR)-D(rho_R||sigma_R),
 J_tau=D((tau tensor id)rho||(tau tensor id)sigma)-D(rho_R||sigma_R).

Only defined finite differences are admitted. Let S be the support of
sum_j tau_j and let Pi_i project, WITHIN S, onto the kernel of
sum_(j!=i)tau_j. Set r_i=Tr(tau_i Pi_i), r=min_i r_i.

**Theorem.** For every admitted pair and every finite R,

    J_tau >= r J_X.                                      (1)

The constant r is SHARP, even restricting R to dimension1 and using
equal-reference hypotheses. Thus the sharp reverse factor is1/r if r>0,
and infinite if r=0. Equivalently,

 D_out >= r D_in+(1-r)D_reference.                        (2)

This does NOT follow merely from D_out>=rD_in. No classical-output
equal-reference/conditional equivalence is imported for these quantum
outputs. The changing-reference term is proved below.

For rational density matrices, kernel projectors, r_i and the sharp factor
are acquired by polynomial exact rational linear algebra. No optimization
over reference states, matrix logarithm or eigenvalue precision oracle is
needed for this operation. Exact supports are substantive input information.

## 2. The algebraic extraction identity

Assume first every r_i>0, and put E_i=Pi_i/r_i. On output Hilbert--Schmidt
space define T(Y)_i=Tr(E_iY), with adjoint T*e_i=E_i. This linear extraction
is NOT claimed to be a jointly normalized POVM.

Positivity implies Pi_i tau_j=tau_j Pi_i=0 for j!=i. Therefore

 T|tau_j>=e_j,
 T L_tau_j T*=T R_tau_j T*=(1/r_j)|j><j|.                 (3)

For example the (i,k) entry of the first identity of operators is
Tr(E_i tau_j E_k): it vanishes unless i=k=j, when it equals
Tr(tau_j Pi_j)/r_j^2=1/r_j. The right-multiplication case follows by
cyclicity of trace with the SAME complex cross terms. The Pi_i need not
be mutually orthogonal. This is precisely why replacing T by an unambiguous
measurement's simultaneous normalization would lose the sharp constant.

For ANY two positive operator families X_i^L,X_i^R on an auxiliary space,
let Q_i=X_i^L+X_i^R and

 W=sum_i L_tau_i tensor X_i^L+R_tau_i tensor X_i^R,
 v=sum_i |tau_i> tensor u_i.

Equation(3) gives

 (T tensor I)W(T* tensor I)=diag(Q_i/r_i),
 (T tensor I)v=col(u_i).

The inverse-form Cauchy inequality, or the variational formula for
v*W^-1v, consequently proves

    <v,W^-1v> >= sum_i r_i<u_i,Q_i^-1u_i>.               (4)

Use faithful weights/restrict to S where necessary; actual modular weights
below are positive. No unsupported one-family CQ Fisher equality is used.

## 3. A direct unequal-reference modular gauge

Take faithful input blocks A_i>0 and Hermitian tangent blocks H_i. Write
M=sum_i A_i, H=sum_i H_i. For s in(0,1), on reference Hilbert--Schmidt
space put

 Q_i=s L_Ai+(1-s)R_Ai, Z=sum_i Q_i,
 z=Z^-1 H, u_i=H_i-Q_i z.

Then sum_i u_i=0 and square completion gives the input conditional
modular Hessian

 sum_i <H_i,Q_i^-1 H_i>-<H,Z^-1H>
      =sum_i <u_i,Q_i^-1u_i>.                           (5)

The output modular operator on HS(S) tensor HS(R) is

 W=s sum_i L_tau_i tensor L_Ai
           +(1-s)sum_i R_tau_i tensor R_Ai.

Its tangent is v_H=sum_i|tau_i> tensor H_i. Because Tr(tau_i)=1,

 W(|I_S> tensor z)=sum_i|tau_i> tensor Q_i z,
 <I_S tensor z,W(I_S tensor z)>=<z,Zz>.

The cross term of v_u=sum_i|tau_i> tensor u_i with I_S tensor z
vanishes by sum_i u_i=0. Thus the output conditional modular Hessian is
EXACTLY

    <v_H,W^-1v_H>-<H,Z^-1H>=<v_u,W^-1v_u>.              (6)

Apply(4) with X_i^L=s L_Ai and X_i^R=(1-s)R_Ai. Equations(5),(6) give
the conditional modular comparison with factor r for EVERY s. Integrate
over s using the ordinary BKM divided-difference representation
g_A(H)=integral_0^1 <H,[sL_A+(1-s)R_A]^-1H> ds.
Then integrate the Hessian along the affine path from sigma to rho with
Taylor weight1-t. The Bregman differences are exactly J_tau and J_X.
This proves(1),(2) for faithful hypotheses with arbitrary reference change.

Finite-divergence boundary hypotheses follow by mixing BOTH with the SAME
faithful cq state on the common input/reference support and passing to the
common-mixture limit. Output space is restricted to S, on which faithful
input blocks give faithful outputs. Infinite-minus-infinite is never used.
If r=0, inequality(1) is simply conditional DPI/nonnegativity; sharpness
is still established next.

## 4. Sharpness with ordinary classical endpoint priors

Fix i. Choose positive weights w_j for j!=i summing to1 and let
omega=sum_(j!=i)w_j tau_j. Compare input rho=|i><i| with the faithful
prior q_i=epsilon, q_j=(1-epsilon)w_j. Their classical divergence is
log(1/epsilon). The output comparison is tau_i versus

    Omega_epsilon=(1-epsilon)omega+epsilon tau_i.

Inside S, Pi_i is exactly ker omega. The compression Pi_i tau_i Pi_i
is positive definite on this kernel: a vector killed by both omega and
tau_i would lie outside S. Small eigenvalues of Omega_epsilon are therefore
Theta(epsilon), with cluster projector Pi_i+O(epsilon); remaining eigenvalues
are bounded away from0. Equivalently, min-max plus
Omega_epsilon>=epsilon(omega+tau_i) for epsilon<=1/2 and the fixed positive
gap of omega on its range gives

    log Omega_epsilon=(log epsilon)Pi_i+O(1).

The cluster-projector error times log epsilon remains bounded. Hence

 D(tau_i||Omega_epsilon)=r_i log(1/epsilon)+O(1).          (7)

The ratio tends to r_i. If Pi_i=0 the output divergence stays bounded,
so the ratio tends to0. These hypotheses have trivial/equal reference;
if faithful rho is desired, regularize it on a smaller scale and use
continuity at each positive epsilon. Equation(7) proves sharpness and
the zero convention without a quantum-reference search or a claimed
favorable rate uniform over channels.

## 5. An explicit finite Choi certificate

The inequality also has a direct coefficient certificate for the two-family
source pencil diag(X_i^L,X_i^R) direct_sum [[W,V],[V*,I]], where
V=sum_i|tau_i> tensor U_i and sum_i U_i=0. The classical-label target is
[[diag(Q_i),U],[U*,cI]], with c=1/r=max_i1/r_i.

Use the arrow Kraus Z/sqrt(c), where Z's upper block is T* and its bottom
entry is c. Its congruence gives target top diag(Q_i/(c r_i)), exact U
offdiagonal and bottom cI. Fill each diagonal deficit
(1-1/(c r_i))Q_i from BOTH corresponding source effect blocks. All fills
are nonnegative. Under the source-first convention
C_(a,p),(b,q)=[Phi(E_ab)]_(p,q), Phi(A)=Z* A Z/c has rank-one Choi matrix
vec(conjugate Z) vec(conjugate Z)*/c, with (a,p) source/output ordering.
These rational outer products and the scalar diagonal fills require no
evaluated square root. Using ZZ* here would have the wrong dimension;
the vectorization/conjugation is essential for complex preparations.
This is a solver-free CP pencil certificate, not a physical degrader.
C independently executed the SAME binary0,+ case's27-order rank1 Choi
coefficient identity in c_cq_extension/EXACT_TWO_FAMILY.json.

## 6. Acquisition, predecessors and limits

Kernel projectors of rational Hermitian matrices are rational: for any
rational full-column kernel basis V use V(V*V)^-1V*. One may compute the
kernel of sum_(j!=i)tau_j in the full output space; the common kernel of
all tau_j contributes zero to r_i and can be subtracted as a nested
projector. Exact rank/linear algebra and traces have polynomial bit cost.
No arbitrary numerical near-zero eigenvalue is declared an exact support.

For independent pure preparations with Gram G, r_i=1/(G^-1)_ii. The sharp
reverse factor is max_i(G^-1)_ii. For |0>,|+>, r=1/2 and it is2. The
ordinary heralded inverse has uniform success1-1/sqrt2, a different physical
operation with weaker bound2+sqrt2. UDM reciprocal states/support subspaces
are established predecessors (Rudolph--Spekkens--Turner2003; Chefles1998),
not new inventions here. B's general pure-pair resolvent proof independently
earns the equal-reference answer; this proof pays the full conditional and
mixed-output operation. Precise broader-world priority remains UNKNOWN.

The exact coefficient is NOT robust under unrestricted channel uncertainty:
any positive full-rank contamination of every preparation makes r=0 for
n>=2. This is a material access boundary, not a physically stable inverse.
The theorem concerns supplied state matrices and a worst-case information
ratio. It does not acquire a quantum experiment, jointly normalized UDM,
capacity, guessing/privacy order, a correlated-block constant or a
civilisation-level operational technology. Product-source retention is
multiplicative at the full product alphabet, as independently derived by B;
it does not make the same single-use reverse factor unchanged under reuse.

## 7. A finite rational witness for a rejected reverse factor

B independently supplied a constructive endpoint bound in
b_mixed_retention_challenge/FINITE_WITNESS.md; root reconstructs the bound
and accepts it at the scope below. This is a separate contributor extension,
not an independently audited numerical entropy-state experiment.

For a proposed finite reverse factor c with c r_i<1, form the rational
uniform mixture omega of all other preparations and P=ker omega within S.
Acquire rational floors 0<a,b<=1 for the positive eigenvalues of
tau_i+omega on S and omega on its range. Rational pseudoinverse traces
give such floors without an orthonormal-basis or spectral oracle. In full
space, A^+=(A+Pker(A))^-1-Pker(A), all rational.

For epsilon<=ab/8, omega_epsilon>=
(epsilon a/2)P+(b/4)(I-P). Operator monotonicity of log and
Tr(tau_i log tau_i)<=0 therefore give the conservative finite bound

    D(tau_i||omega_epsilon)
       <=r_i log(1/epsilon)+log(8/(ab)).

One may see the matrix lower bound directly by writing
omega_epsilon=epsilon(tau_i+omega)+(1-2epsilon)omega and using the two
acquired floors; no unjustified eigenvector alignment is required.
Choose integer h with2^h>=8/(ab), then an integer k>=h with
k>c h/(1-c r_i). The rational priors p=e_i and
q_i=2^-k,q_j=(1-2^-k)/(n-1) give STRICT

    D_input=k log2 > c D_output.

Thus the returned finite pair certifies rejection without evaluating any
logarithm. It has trivial reference, finite divergences and a faithful q;
p is a permitted boundary input. If r_i=0 the same operation works for
every finite c. The bit length k of this explicit witness may be large
in the gap1-c r_i and conditioning. Polynomial acquisition of the sharp
coefficient is not a polynomial short-witness claim in their logarithms.

## Primary material actually read

* Rudolph--Spekkens--Turner, *Unambiguous discrimination of mixed states*,
  Phys.Rev.A68,010301(R)(2003), arXiv:quant-ph/0303071v2,
  https://arxiv.org/html/quant-ph/0303071v2 , SectionsI--III. It states
  the private-kernel condition, formulates mixed-state discrimination
  as a POVM SDP, and gives the pure two-state optimal success formula.
  Thus the support geometry and qualitative possibility of heralded
  inversion are established prior.
* Hirche, *Quantum Doeblin coefficients: A simple upper bound on
  contraction coefficients*, arXiv:2405.00105v2,
  https://arxiv.org/html/2405.00105 , SectionIV. Its reverse Doeblin
  program supplies expansion bounds, chiefly for trace distance; it
  does not identify arbitrary relative-entropy expansion with that
  trace-distance bound.
* George--Hirche--Nuradha--Wilde, *Quantum Doeblin Coefficients:
  Interpretations and Applications*, Quantum10,2115(22May2026),
  https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-05-22-2115 , with primary full text
  https://arxiv.org/html/2503.22823v3 , Section6.2/Definition13 and
  Proposition33. This defines complete expansion with equal-reference
  hypotheses and bounds complete TRACE-distance expansion by reverse
  Doeblin. That inspected statement is not the new proposed Umegaki
  private-weight formula.
* Belzig--Gao--Smith--Wu, *Reverse-type Data Processing Inequality*,
  arXiv:2411.19890v3, https://arxiv.org/html/2411.19890v3 , Section4.1
  and Lemma4.1 were read during the preceding pure-pair investigation.
  BKM comparison followed by line integration is standard machinery.
  Its unrestricted quantum-input no-reverse theorem is not a
  classical-input-algebra theorem.

This is a targeted primary comparison, not an exhaustive priority
clearance. Historical novelty remains UNKNOWN. C independently reads
Eriksson AIRR v3 for complete maximum-contraction/activation; that
source is not treated as this reviewer's completed full-paper intake.

## Strong ordinary construction on the SAME information

With private weights r_i>0, standard unambiguous discrimination already
produces a finite heralded inverse. One explicit success probability is
`p=1/||sum_i P_i/r_i||`, with POVM effects `p P_i/r_i`; numerical
optimization of the POVM may improve it. Instrument DPI gives
`J_tau>=p J_id`, even with changing reference marginals, because the
failure flag then carries exactly the reference marginal. Every
uniform-success unambiguous instrument has p<=rmin. For two pure
outputs with overlap s, the optimal p is1-s, whereas rmin=1-s^2.

The proposed operation replaces this possibly nonsharp physical
success bound by the exact Umegaki coefficient, while retaining full
conditional semantics and arbitrary finite reference dimensions. It
does so by a Hilbert--Schmidt projection whose individual effects
cannot generally form one POVM. That distinction is mathematically
substantive, but it is not a superior physical label-recovery device.

## What must remain separate

The formula would solve the minimum-retention question for finite cq
preparations on exact input matrices. It does not solve arbitrary
pairwise CQ channel comparison, prove necessity of the general
two-unrestricted-family SDP condition, or grant a finite reference
cutoff in other comparison problems. It gives neither a quantum
capacity advantage nor a practical experiment without calibration.

Full-rank contamination makes the universal reverse factor infinite,
even at arbitrarily small contamination. Hence exact support admission
is genuinely required. Restricting priors, changing the loss to a
fixed-reference one, or asking for additive approximate inversion
would lead to different potentially robust operations; no such
replacement is silently included.

No new numerical source, channel, bath, dynamics, or search was
acquired/executed for this challenge. The independent reconstruction
and upcoming whole-file intake are analytical. Read-only primary
retrieval and existing peer sources were the only acquisition.

I developed a causal mechanism for reusing syndrome registers, together with a more general bound based on physical accuracy. The intended capability is repeated correction with a smaller supply of clean memory, while preserving the information carried by returning environments.

The construction works under additional, explicit assumptions about the noise generator and the protection of the archive. It has a working finite implementation; it does not yet supply a practical device advantage or a noisy-control threshold.

1. A register that is actually returned for reuse

After each correction round, a reversible operation transfers the coherent syndrome into an archive and returns the temporary syndrome register to  $|0\rangle$ . The next round receives that actual register. The archive retains the history’s correlations with the bath and arbitrary reference systems.

I derived a bound allowing an unknown, repeated finite-bath interaction, interrupted at up to  $r$  positions by arbitrary interactions with other retained memory. Those exceptional interactions can revisit the same memory, fail to commute, and appear in coherent combinations. Their locations do not have to be detected.

The binary specialization has an exact answer. If ordinary rounds emit the same unknown coherent syndrome, the required archive dimension is $D_{n,r}
=
\sum_{k=0}^{r}
(n-2k+1)
\left[
\binom nk-\binom n{k-1}
\right],
\qquad r\le \lfloor n/2\rfloor .$ 

An incremental Schur construction implements the compression during the correction loop. Within the requirement to preserve this entire history family reversibly, the dimension is also necessary.

For illustration, the formula gives:

 | Correction rounds | Permitted departures from the repeated generator | Archive qubits

 | 1,000 | 0 | 10

 | 1,000 | 1 | 20

 | 1,000 | 2 | 29

These are resource calculations, not 1,000-round device simulations. Each row additionally requires the reused syndrome qubit, the source, control and arithmetic workspace, and reliable holding of the archive. Here  $r$  counts changes to the interaction structure; it is not the number of observed logical errors.

2. The stronger opening: accuracy changes the memory requirement

An exact-only approach has a serious failure.

Even with one unknown parameter, no active bath, and bounded total interaction time, varying the timings can produce a syndrome family whose exact span has dimension  $2^n$ . Thus “few unknown physical parameters” alone does not justify small exact storage.

I then derived an approximate causal construction. Its archive size depends on how many representative physical models are needed to cover the unknown model class at the required whole-program accuracy.

With no exceptional interactions, the bound is $m_{\mathrm{archive}}
\le
\left\lceil
2\log_2 d+\log_2 N_\delta
\right\rceil ,$ 

where  $d$  is the active bath dimension and  $N_\delta$  is a covering number defined using the accumulated sensitivity of the actual physical operations.

For a bounded,  $p$ -parameter Hamiltonian family, this yields a bound of the form $m_{\mathrm{archive}}
=
O\!\left(
p\log(1+L/\delta)+\log d
\right),$ 

where  $L$  measures the integrated sensitivity to those parameters.

The compressor does not first estimate the unknown coupling. It works for the declared model family. The error proof compares the complete recycled circuits and retains any imperfectly cleared intermediate register in the actual evolution. It grants no fresh bath or intermediate initialization.

This is the most promising conceptual result of the investigation: the physical accuracy requirement can make a reusable controller possible even when exact universal compression requires the entire raw history. The general construction is analytic; its efficient, robust synthesis remains unresolved.

3. What the executable construction establishes

The implemented example runs 12 correction rounds, with two interactions involving the same noncommuting, reference-entangled memory. Its physical source has a dirty-input completion that can flip the logical state. That action remains present throughout the simulation.

The positive run produced:

Complete history–bath–reference reconstruction error of approximately  $4.42\times10^{-16}$ .

Logical Bell fidelity approximately  $1$  throughout.

Return of the reused syndrome register to zero within floating-point tolerance.

Separate checks cover an exact rational restoration identity and four exact modular span ranks.

The negative case matters equally. When a compiler allowing no exceptional interaction encounters one, its supposedly cleared register has nonzero probability  $1/2$ . Continuing the real circuit with that register reduces logical Bell fidelity to  $1/2$ . The construction therefore preserves the earlier dirty-input failure rather than concealing it in a reference process.

Unknown repeated tensor-network states already admit logarithmic compression, and efficient Schur transforms are established constructions. Those predecessors redirected this investigation toward live reuse, returning-memory interventions, and accuracy-dependent control; their underlying compression results are not new Astra discoveries. hub.hku.hk+1 Standard non-Markovian fault-tolerance machinery also remains prior. arxiv.org

The current construction additionally assumes a valid model class, coherent recovery, an isolated archive, and sufficiently accurate compression gates. The inherited bridge does not establish those conditions. no singular value of the UNKNOWN P basis is inverted. The retained-coordinate
condition is bounded by the known truncation threshold. To make finite arithmetic
literal, retain a rational approximate spectral subspace and perform exact
rational volume swaps on its coordinate columns. If the retained dimension is
d<=r, their initial volume is at least(delta_svd/sqrt(N))^d; with coordinate
norms<=R the selected-basis inverse can cost O(d log(d N R/delta_svd)) bits.
The factor d (hence r) is explicitly internal arithmetic cost, not a target
singular-value premise or a new teacher-precision oracle. Cache/subspace errors
enlarge the ideal residual constant4 to at most6; since N>=x^60 this is still
below zeta/10. See JOINT_RESTRICTIONS and A's independent fresh-side challenge.

Independently of any selected coefficients, a finite net for [-4,4]^N and
Hoeffding preserve the full L1 norm of EVERY teacher-row combination to zeta/10.
Consequently each sampled q_i is within zeta/2 of a combination of the selected
Q rows. Combine with the hidden true population spanner: outside gamma0 P-mass,
p_h is within r zeta of a combination of selected q's, coefficients<=2r. Its
mass differs from1 by at most r zeta. Normalize its coefficients by that mass:
the resulting signed density z0 has mass1, coefficients<=3r and

    ||p_h-z0||_1<=4r zeta.                            (2)

All selected rows are FRESH Q conditionals. Neither previous-basis children nor
their teacher error enter the selection or its importance measure.

## 3. Fresh features, positivity in measure and feasible proxies

Append a uniform row to the selected rows, R_1,...,R_S, S<=r+1, and set
mu=sum R_i/S. Then R_i/mu<=S and mu>=1/(S O^L), L remaining length. Draw D NEW
features from mu, independently after all basis choices. Coefficients satisfy
sum alpha=1, |alpha_i|<=C and finite-feature density z_alpha/mu>=tau. Uniform
coefficients are strictly feasible. At finite precision the implemented threshold
is2tau with slack, while the following statements concern exact virtual rows.

The full negative mass of every feasible state is at most v, simultaneously over
ALL possible inference choices. To see this, apply uniform Hoeffding/net bounds
to (-sum alpha_i R_i/mu)_+. Its empirical negative mass is0, its envelope<=SC,
and its coefficient sup-norm Lipschitz constant<=S^2. The sample count D pays
uniform error v (with half reserved for arithmetic). This is a negative-MASS
bound, not global pointwise positivity inferred from finitely many tests.

Pad the proxy (2) towards mu with weight4tau. It has mass1, coefficients<C and
L1 error e<=4r zeta+8tau<=9tau. If the unpadded density is>=-tau mu at a feature,
the padded density is>=3tau mu. Violating that condition has mu-probability at
most4r zeta/tau. Conditional on all acquired geometry, the expected P-prefix mass
without a feature-feasible proxy is at most gamma0+4D r zeta/tau<=d'tau/20.
Markov over the fresh features gives bad P-prefix mass<=tau except with
probability d'/20. This is P-weighted coverage of ACTUAL histories. It never
conditions on a previously selected basis prefix, avoiding the failed bias step.

## 4. Arbitrary child restrictions enter only a clipped logarithm

At the next cut cache V_(i,o)(f)=R_i(o,f), evaluated on that cut's features.
Each V is a subprobability density<=1. For a current state alpha and actual token
probability pi_o>=a, its reference is w_o=sum alpha_i V_(i,o)/pi_o. No normalized
Q(.|h_i o) query is needed. Bounds below allow every such child without any rank,
target-closeness or coverage promise. Its coefficient box is C/a.

Use delta_L=theta a^L and [z]_L=max(z,delta_L). The floor's total added mass is
at most theta. Every feasible state has excess k_z=int([z]_L-z)<=v+theta.
Let K=(r+1)C/a+2 and B=log[K/(theta a^T)]. Clipped densities lie between delta_L
and K, their pairwise log ratios have magnitude<=B, and their total clipped
masses are at most K.

Uniformly over bounded alpha0,alpha,beta, the function

    ((z_alpha0-z_alpha)/mu) log([z_alpha]_L/[w_beta]_L)

has envelope2SCB and coefficient sup-norm Lipschitz constant at most
2S^2 B+2SC(S+k)/delta_L, k<=r+1 for each token. A coefficient net followed by
Hoeffding therefore integrates it to error xi. Although the floor is exponentially
small in T, ONLY the logarithm of that Lipschitz constant enters the sample
count. No child-dominating importance measure is required. The features remain
independent of all bases; uniformity covers adaptive future coefficient choices.

For the current raw reference w, minimize the finite convex objective

    J(alpha)=D^-1 sum_j [z_alpha(f_j)/mu(f_j)
                         *log(z_alpha(f_j)/[w]_L(f_j))
                         -z_alpha(f_j)/mu(f_j)] .     (3)

Its first-order residual is at most xi. The minus-linear term is necessary
because normalization is in the FULL space, not the empirical feature sum.
Uniform integration gives int(z0-z)log([z]_L/[w]_L)>=-2xi. For a true p and a
feasible proxy z0 with ||p-z0||1<=e, put
Phi_L(p,z)=int p log(p/[z]_L), Z_w=int[w]_L. Then

    Phi_L(p,z)<=Phi_L(p,w)+log Z_w+2xi+B(e+2k_z).      (4)

Proof: insert z0, costing eB, and use the first-order inequality. Replacing z
by [z]_L costs Bk_z. Log-sum gives int[z]_L log([w]_L/[z]_L)
<=(1+k_z)log(Z_w/(1+k_z)). Subtracting log Z_w leaves at most Bk_z since
Z_w<=K. This establishes (4) without a pointwise-positive full signed state.

At bad histories, Phi_L(p,z)-Phi_L(p,w)<=B directly from the clipped log bound.

## 5. Exact transition normalization retains token KL

At a state of exact mass1 and negative mass<=v, let m_o=int z(o,f). Output

    pi_o=max(m_o,b)/M0, M0=sum_o max(m_o,b).

Here1<=M0<=1+v+O b<=2 and pi_o>=a. The raw child is w_o=z(o,.)/pi_o. As
pi_o delta_(L-1)>=delta_L, the exact unnormalized chain rule gives

    sum_o p(o)Phi_(L-1)(p(.|o),w_o)
       <=Phi_L(p,z)-D(p_tokens||pi).                 (5)

The child normalization is uniformly near1, independent of its coverage:

    Z_wo<=m_o/pi_o+v/pi_o+theta
          <=1+v+O b+v/a+theta,
    log Z_wo<=v+O b+v/a+theta<=4tau.                 (6)

The last direct bound is essential: a different Jensen normalization bound can
cancel the token KL and would not prove a compiler. Every projection resets the
parent negative mass to v, so v/a=tau never recurses through T. Token cache
rounding changes (6) by the explicit small terms in JOINT_RESTRICTIONS; (5)
holds for any actual positive pi and remains EXACT for that actual token rule.

Initialize with (1-tau)Q+tau U, whose Phi<=Delta+2tau and negative mass0. Its
required marginal/joint feature data are also cached. At the empty future the
only state is1 and Phi=0. Apply (4)-(6), average under the FIXED P prefix law,
and sum over cuts. The good-proxy error<=9tau, bad mass<=tau and floor/negative
errors give

    D(P||P_hat)<=Delta+2tau+T[6tau+12B tau].          (7)

The sum of token KLs is the KL of the ENTIRE output law by chain rule. There is
no selected-child coverage, P conditional oracle, inverse target-state matrix,
or recursively worsened teacher error in (7). With finite arithmetic, value-
oracle error, known Slater slack and convex-solve residual reserves, use

    D(P||P_hat)<=Delta+40T(B+1)tau.                  (8)

## 6. Explicit resource domination

For x>=1000 the schedule has d'>=x^-2, tau>=x^-1, a>=x^-1 and theta>=x^-1;
A,r+1,O,T,C<=x. It follows successively that D<=x^41, zeta>=x^-50,
N<=x^61, M<=x^1200, theta_geo>=x^-112 and eta>=x^-1400. Therefore
Delta<=x^-4096 makes the good-row failure at most2x^-1234, well inside delta.
The exact bound NM eta/theta_geo<=d'/100 pays the pointwise geometry error.

For sample-compression, gamma0>=x^-4 gives gamma0(N-r)>=x^56/2, while
log[(r+1)N^r/(d'/100)]<=x^3. Thus N pays its failure probability. For the full
L1 sketch a coefficient net gives a bound below10^9 N^7 zeta^-3 (including
confidence); (A N/zeta)^10 dominates it since A>=1000 and N>=1,zeta<=1.

For the gradient sketch use B<=A log x<=x^2, envelope<=x^5, parameter dimension
<=x^2, net log per coordinate<=x^2 and confidence log<=x. With half tolerances
and fixed constants the sufficient Hoeffding bound is below x^24. The negative-
mass bound has a smaller majorant because1/v<=x^2. D=ceil(x^40) pays both, and
the additional token/cut union only changes their confidence log. Across all
events the allocated failure is less than delta, including finite conditional-
sample implementation failures.

Geometry is computed at polynomial BIT accuracy around a known truncation
threshold. Inference (3) has bounded gradient and Hessian polynomial in S,B,1/tau;
the rational coefficient polytope has a known uniform Slater point. A linear-
minimization/Frank--Wolfe procedure decreases its bounded objective by a polynomial
multiple of the squared first-order gap. Ordinary rational LPs and warranted log
intervals therefore produce gap<=tau in polynomial time. No installed SVD or
CLARABEL run is presumed to certify these worst-case statements.

Each full row/joint density evaluation uses at most T next-token calls. The
compilation count is bounded by a fixed polynomial, for example a constant
multiple of T^2[NM+(O+1)(r+1)D+M+D], plus geometric/convex arithmetic. The output
stores O[T O(r+1)D] density/marginal scalars; optional feature-string provenance
adds O(T^2 D log O) bits and is not needed by inference. Scalar bit lengths
are polynomial in T log(O/a),logN,logM,logD,log(1/tau). During inference only
these finite arrays, a bounded rational coefficient vector and convex programs
are used. There is no hidden Q call. Its service cost is nevertheless fully paid
at compilation; probability VALUES, not sample-only access, are load-bearing.

## 7. Choose tau and derive the stated error

Take dyadic tau_acc between (epsilon/(1024A^2))^4 and twice that value. Start
tau=tau_acc and first compare the supplied rational Delta with (tau_acc/A)^4096.
If it is no larger, KEEP tau_acc: do not compute a tiny root of Delta. Otherwise
double tau until Delta<=(tau/A)^4096, or tau>1/(100A). This uses only
O(log(1/tau_acc)) exact rational comparisons, with the supplied input length
L_in charged. When nontrivial doubling occurs, tau<2A Delta^(1/4096).
All output parameters therefore have bit length controlled by tau_acc, not by
an arbitrarily tiny Delta denominator. If tau>1/(100A), return uniform independent
tokens. In this case the right side of(1) exceeds1: tau_acc cannot cause it and
the preceding unsuccessful comparison was at tau/2>1/(200A), so
Delta^(1/16384)>(1/(200A^2))^(1/4).

Otherwise Delta<=(tau/A)^4096 and all resource gates above apply. Since
B<=A log(A/tau), (8) and Pinsker imply the conservative bound

    TV(P,P_hat)<=sqrt(Delta/2)+10A^2 tau^(1/4).

Use tau<=max(tau_acc,2A Delta^(1/4096)) to obtain(1), with room for its
constants. Tau>=tau_acc bounds ALL sample counts and sizes by a fixed polynomial
in A,1/epsilon, regardless of how tiny Delta is. T does not appear in the
exponents of epsilon or Delta. No claim of useful moderate-Delta constants follows.

## 8. Source, execution and unsolved qualifications

Liu--Moitra2411.07536v1, §§3,5,6,7 is the strongest consumed constructive source:
same-target conditional queries, bounded barycentric geometry, density-mixture
sketches, robust truncation and KL convex inference are established machinery.
The new proposed interface is fresh-P acquisition under global KL to a different
arbitrary-rank teacher, coupled to signed full states and the asymmetric clipped-
log telescope. A same-target learner cannot be transferred merely by renaming Q.
Historical priority of this particular extension has not been established.

The retained T8 engineering run uses MUCH smaller budgets and floating tools.
It checks access separation and finite caching, not(1). The rank2 target/rank16
teacher diagnostic, all output probabilities, counts, first failed implementation,
corrected run and ordinary two-component EM comparison remain visible. The EM
model has narrower structural knowledge and no Q calls; it was dramatically
faster. No best-incumbent computational advantage is asserted. The proof itself
remains PROPOSED pending independent whole challenge.

# Joint restrictions and literal finite-precision access

30 October 2026. This strengthens/simplifies the proposed compiler's access
implementation. It replaces the normalized-child cache in the engineering
prototype and the support-cutoff construction in RESOURCE_QUALIFICATION §4.
The existing execution is preserved; this note does not claim a second run.

## 1. Do not divide a teacher child

For a selected positive-Q prefix h_i, store at the next cut's feature f_j the
JOINT restriction

    V_(i,o)(f_j) = Q(o f_j | h_i).

For the uniform row the value is O^(-L), where L is the parent's remaining
length. Each V_(i,o) is a subprobability density on child futures, bounded by1.
Its mass is the separately stored q_i(o). Its value is a product of next-token
probabilities starting at h_i. It never requires a query at h_i o.

Given parent coefficients alpha and the ACTUALLY OUTPUT token probability pi_o,
the reference array is

    w_o(f_j) = sum_i alpha_i V_(i,o)(f_j) / pi_o.

This is exactly the restriction of the virtual full signed parent density,
divided by pi_o. Coefficients are bounded by C/a. The asymmetric gradient lemma
uses only 0<=V_i<=1, integral V_i<=1 and a bounded coefficient box; it therefore
holds unchanged. No child is sampled, placed into the importance mixture, or
required to approximate a target conditional law. If q_i(o)=0 its entire joint
restriction is zero. No zero-probability conditional oracle is needed.

## 2. A full-future probability at finite precision

At a positive-Q prefix h the product for a fixed continuation f has factors in
[0,1]. Request each next-token factor to absolute accuracy eps/(8T). Track an
outward interval for the partial product. Before querying an extension, either
its partial product has certified positive lower endpoint, or its upper endpoint
is at most eps/2. In the latter case return0: the final product is at most eps/2.
If neither condition holds, refine the current factor. A value that stays
unresolved within the requested factor precision forces the partial product to
be at most eps/2 after adjusting the constants. Thus the algorithm does not need
to decide whether an arbitrary tiny probability is exactly zero.

A more literal fixed-budget implementation uses next-token intervals of width
eps/(16T) from the start: if an extension's lower endpoint is nonpositive, its
upper probability is at most eps/(8T), so STOP rather than query it. Its final
product is then at most eps/(8T). Otherwise the extension is certified positive.
Products of all non-stopped factors have error at most the sum of widths. All
teacher queries are at known positive-Q prefixes. Every sampled raw basis prefix
is positive-Q because P(h)>0 and D(P||Q)<infinity. This is a consequence of the
supplied promise, not a test by the learner.

Both V_(i,o) and the fresh full-row densities can therefore be cached to arbitrary
absolute eps using polynomially many queries and O(log(T/eps)) probability bits.
This is a VALUE-ORACLE result. Its service cost must be charged at that precision.
It is NOT a polynomial conditional-SAMPLE-only simulation: estimating an
exponentially small absolute tolerance from draws can take exponentially many.

## 3. Robust cache, constraints and the real transition

Let eps be a uniform absolute error bound for every cached row density, joint
restriction and token probability. Normalize the token rows as rational
probability vectors with l1 error<=2O eps. Put E_m=2S C O eps. Then the actual
computed marginals mhat have sum1 and satisfy |mhat_o-m_o|<=E_m. The actual token
rule uses max(mhat_o,b), normalized. Its denominator is at most

    1+v+O b+O E_m,

since the true signed token marginals have negative mass at most v. If the
displayed excess is<=1, every actual pi_o>=b/2=a. Moreover the TRUE virtual
reference normalization satisfies

    integral max(z(o,.)/pi_o,delta_child)
       <=1+v+O b+O E_m+E_m/a+v/a+theta_floor.

This is the only place token-row rounding changes the transition normalization
proof. The exact chain-rule inequality holds for ANY actual positive pi, hence
has no additional approximation term. There is no sequence of inferred teacher
conditional-error divisions.

For mixture floor mu_min=1/(S O^L), the true feature ratios R_i/mu are at most S.
Store rational approximations rhat_i and define muhat=sum_i rhat_i/S EXACTLY.
For eps<=mu_min/4 the ratio error is at most 4S eps/mu_min per row. Thus all
coefficient-state feature values differ from their true values by at most
4S^2 C eps/mu_min. Impose the rational constraint zhat/muhat>=2tau. The true
padded proxy is>=3tau at good features and the true values of all feasible
states are>=tau when the last error is<=tau/2. The uniform coefficient vector
is strictly feasible with ratio exactly1. Sum alpha=1 is imposed exactly, so
the virtual full signed density has mass exactly1 regardless of rounding.

At child features the raw reference value has error at most S C eps/a.
Clipping and log are Lipschitz with constants1 and1/delta_min. The empirical
gradient discrepancy is bounded by a polynomial in S,C,1/a,1/mu_min,
1/delta_min,B times eps. Choose eps so that this bound, O E_m+E_m/a, and all
ratio errors use at most tau/100 each. For example a sufficiently conservative
single value is

    eps = [tau a delta_min mu_min /
           (10^6 (S+1)(C+1)(O+1)(T+1)(B+1))]^4.

One may replace B by the explicit rational integer upper bound A*ceil(log2 x)
times2, avoiding a transcendental request in the accuracy rule. Finite interval
evaluation/LP certificates pay the same remaining tolerance. The bit length is
polynomial in T,log O,log(1/tau),log D,log N,log M. The tiny VALUE of eps is not
a polynomial-in-1/eps query-count claim: the primitive supplies requested
probability BITS, whose actual service cost is explicitly multiplied in.

Geometry has its own preliminary tolerance. With
mu_geo_min=1/((N+1)O^L), request density error at most
theta_geo*mu_geo_min/[1000(N+1)]. This changes the ratio columns by at most
theta_geo/100, fitting inside the robust-SVD constants in FRESH_SPANNERS. Its
bit length is again polynomial. It is not omitted from the value-oracle bill.

## 4. Sampling features and output tokens

Conditional Q-sampling is already an input primitive. If instead it is implemented
from next-token probability queries, draw a persistent uniform and compare it
with the categorical cumulative sums using successively refined intervals. An
exact chosen token has positive Q probability almost surely, so every subsequent
conditional call is valid. Here b bits means the cumulative probabilities have
width O(2^-b): request b+ceil(log2 O)+3 bits for EACH token probability before
summing. The probability that a comparison remains unresolved at that cumulative
precision is at most 2O*2^-b. Across a prescribed polynomial number of calls,
truncate at a known polynomial bit budget and count any unresolved outcome as
a declared compilation failure. A union bound fits this inside delta/10.
This avoids silently sampling an impossible prefix by rounding a zero upward.

The returned finite model uses rational token probabilities and no Q reference.
They can be sampled with expected polynomial fair-bit work, or with a finite bit
budget and separately allocated TV error. The teaching oracle's own numerical
complexity and the full-trajectory source's acquisition cost are inputs, not free
physical measurement capabilities.

## 5. Status

These are mathematical access/perturbation statements for the general proposed
compiler. The finite engineering run used normalized child arrays, floating SVD
and CLARABEL, with a full-support teacher, and hence did not exercise support-zero
or formal interval branches. Its output is not a verified implementation of the
formal astronomical resource schedule. The proof still awaits independent whole
challenge; no practical advantage or installed-library worst-case complexity is
claimed.

# Resource and finite-precision qualification for the proposed compiler

This closes the parameter interfaces in the proposed proof; independent whole
review is pending. None of the formal budgets is advertised as practical.

## 1. One polynomial, not a recursion in the horizon

Use A,x,tau,d',D,gamma0,zeta,N,M,theta_geo,eta exactly as in FRESH_SPANNERS5.
Every cut uses the SAME bounds. For A>=1000 and0<tau<=1/(100A):

    d'>=x^-2, zeta>=x^-50, gamma0>=x^-4,
    N<=x^61, M<=x^1200, theta_geo>=x^-112,
    eta>=x^-1400.                                    (1)

Here D<=x^41 since ceil(x^40)<=2x^40<=x^41. Also100(r+1)<=A and
100T<=A, and tau>=x^-1. These inequalities immediately give zeta>=x^-46;
the weaker x^-50 leaves room. A N/zeta<=x^112 implies M<=x^1121<=x^1200.
Then theta_geo>=x^-112 and the second term of eta is at least x^-1376.
The first term is at least x^-51. This proves(1).

N also pays the population sample-compression event: r/gamma0<=x^5 and
log(1/d')<=2log x, so the predecessor's already generous
(r/gamma0)^10 log(1/d') is below x^60. Alternatively substitute into the explicit
union bound(r+1)N^r exp[-gamma0(N-r)]; the negative exponent dominates because
gamma0(N-r)>=x^56/2 whereas its logarithmic competitor is at most O(x^2).

M=(A N/zeta)^10 dominates the full-L1 row-sketch Hoeffding/net bound. For coefficient
boxes[-4,4]^N the envelope is<=8N² and the sup-norm Lipschitz constant<=2N².
A zeta/(100N²) net has logarithm<=N log(1+800N²/zeta). The needed sample count
is bounded by a constant times N^7 zeta^-3 plus the confidence term; the stated
power10 exceeds it because A>=1000. Uniform row proximity in the sketch fails
with probability<=N M eta/theta_geo<=d'/100.

The global teacher event fails with probability<=2 T N Delta/eta². If
Delta<=x^-4096, (1) bounds this by2x^-1234 (or a still smaller bound), below the
allocated confidence. Equivalently it is much stronger than the explicit
d'eta²/(100TN) condition. No term tau^-T enters this probability calculation.

## 2. D pays the asymmetric projection events

The full density floor is delta_L=theta_floor a^L, theta_floor=tau/[4(r+1)]
and a=tau/(2O). Let K=(r+1)C/a+2. On all cuts

    B=log(K/(theta_floor a^T))<=A log x.

A coefficient sup-net for the clipped-gradient class has dimension at most
2(r+1)+O(r+1), if all child families are included together. The larger family
only adds a polynomial factor; it does not need a child sampling measure. Its
envelope is2S C B. The Lipschitz constant contains1/delta_L, but only its LOG
appears in the net size. Since T<=A, that log is O(A log x). The Hoeffding/net
sample bound is conservatively below x^24, including confidence and constant
factors; D=ceil(x^40) exceeds it.

For negative mass, the envelope is S C and coefficient Lipschitz constant S².
The desired error v=a tau has inverse<=x^4. Its analogous sample bound is below
x^24 too. Use half the allotted errors for the exact-data concentration and leave
the remaining halves for arithmetic. Multiplying these bounds by fixed constants
still lies below x^40 at x>=1000.

For feature-positive proxies, Section3 of FRESH_SPANNERS gives expected bad
P-prefix mass<=gamma0+4D r zeta/tau<=d'tau/20. Markov therefore bounds the chance
that its actual bad mass exceeds tau by d'/20. This is conditional on the acquired
basis, with a NEW independent feature sample. Across cuts and the other events,
the failure budget is below delta. Generated-history dependence is covered by
uniform coefficient events; it is not an additional union over exponentially
many prefixes.

## 3. No spectral conditioning oracle

In geometry, the unknown true-row sketch has rank<=r and the computed sketch is
within the stated known norm perturbation. Singular values above twice that
perturbation can be retained; those below can be discarded at paid L1 error.
If a singular value lies on a proposed threshold, choose a threshold gap among
r+1 levels between2 and4 times the perturbation, at spacing polynomially small
relative to it. Approximate SVD to that precision identifies a valid gap. The
smallest retained singular value then has a KNOWN lower bound. Pivot construction
and volume-doubling take polynomially many steps in its logarithm. Relaxing the
swap/stop thresholds by fixed factors pays finite arithmetic without deciding
equality of unknown real singular values. Constants in zeta/100 leave this room.
In a literal finite realization retain a rational approximate spectral subspace
and run exact rational volume swaps in its coordinate matrix. The selected basis
can have inverse bit conditioning O(d log(dNR/delta_svd)), d<=r: this r factor is
paid internal arithmetic, not a teacher-value accuracy or target-gap oracle.
Subspace/cache errors replace the ideal residual constant4 by at most6, still
below zeta/10 since N>=x^60. A's independent fresh-side derivation supplies this
same qualification; no new schedule is needed.

This is ordinary robust-spanner machinery with its actual hypotheses supplied;
it is not a new exact-rank oracle or free inverse of a target singular value.

## 4. Probability precision and teacher support

Every sketch measure includes a uniform future, so its density is at least
1/((N+1)O^L) in geometry and1/((r+1)O^L) in projection. Thus cached ratios can be
evaluated to any required accuracy with an absolute probability request having
only O(L log O) additional bits. Products of next-token probabilities have
absolute error bounded by the sum of their individual errors.

All raw basis prefixes are P-sampled and have positive Q probability when Delta
is finite. If the Q interface only supports positive-probability histories,
there is still no need for a zero-prefix query: child rows with next probability
below c_cut are replaced by the known uniform conditional, retaining their next
token mass. Heavy children have a certified positive probability and may be
queried. Choose c_cut<=tau a delta_min/[1000 S C O], where
delta_min=theta_floor a^T. The resulting full restriction error is at most
2S C O c_cut; after division by p_hat>=a and clipping the log its effect is at
most O(S C O c_cut/(a delta_min))<=tau/100. This is a precision bill, not a
division of conditional teacher error at each depth.

A queried future product can stop before an unsupported extension once its
partial product is below its required absolute tolerance. Otherwise refinement
certifies a positive partial product before requesting the next conditional.
At a true zero, the former event settles at the known tolerance; at a value above
tolerance, the latter settles. Only polynomially many precision bits are needed.
No unacquired total conditional P oracle or Q sample from an impossible history
is thereby granted.

Finite conditional-sampling accuracy, if the primitive is not exact, is allocated
across the known polynomial number of feature draws by coupling/union bound. Its
requested error and ACTUAL service cost must be charged. It is not automatically
obtained from a pointwise probability response at no computational cost.

## 5. Finite cached arrays and convex inference

Take all density/marginal cache errors small enough that their propagated error
through division by the known mixture floors and clipped logs is<=tau/100 per
step. A sufficient accuracy is a fixed polynomial in tau,a,delta_min, the mixture
floor,1/D,1/N,1/M and1/(S C O T). Its BIT LENGTH is polynomial in
T log(O/a), log(1/tau),logN,logM,logD. Absolute errors may be exponentially small
in T; their bit requirement is not exponential in T.

Store normalized rational next-token rows, so their row sums are exactly1.
Their discrepancy from the underlying teacher rows is included in the preceding
restriction/log budget. Use empirical feature lower constraint2tau with arithmetic
slack: the true padded proxy is>=3tau, while every accepted coefficient state has
true feature density>=tau. Uniform coefficients give empirical value1 and known
Slater slack. Coefficient sums are imposed exactly; the virtual full density's
mass is therefore1 even when off-feature entries are signed.

The empirical generalized-KL objective's Hessian is bounded by a polynomial in
S and1/tau, and its gradient by a polynomial in S,B. Linear minimization over
the rational coefficient polytope is an ordinary polynomial-size LP. Short-step
Frank--Wolfe decreases the objective by at least a polynomial multiple of the
squared dual gap; its bounded objective range therefore permits a polynomial
iteration bound to a certified first-order gap<=tau. Log evaluations at paid
precision and a conservative gap tolerance suffice. This is a constructive
convex inference operation, not an unspecified nonlinear global-fit oracle.

The model stores only the finite feature strings/arrays, next-token rows,
parameters and inference algorithm. The full teacher row densities in the proof
are virtual mathematical witnesses, NEVER post-compilation evaluation resources.
Rational categorical token probabilities can be sampled exactly in finite expected
bit time, or with a bounded randomness budget and a separately allocated TV error.

## 6. Current status

These are detailed derivations of the access/precision/resource gates, not a claim
that an installed SVD/convex package has been validated at the formal astronomical
sample schedule. Root/peer whole challenge is still needed before accepting the
proposed full theorem. Practical compiler implementation, usefulness at moderate
Delta, and advantage against the best equally informed conventional learner remain
separate. No physical/native world-model acquisition is claimed.
The ordinary encoded length of supplied rational Delta,epsilon,delta is charged
in input/arithmetic cost. First compare Delta with (tau_acc/A)^4096. If it is no
larger, use tau_acc directly; otherwise double tau until its known teacher-error
condition or the uniform fallback holds. Thus no output-precision dependence on
an unnecessarily tiny Delta is hidden in a root computation. See governing
PROOF Section7; the original COMPILER_DRAFT root description is historical.
