# Proposed teacher-free compiler by asymmetric signed KL projection

30 October 2026. This is a COMPLETE PROPOSED MATHEMATICAL CONSTRUCTION, pending
independent whole challenge. Neither the engineering execution nor this label is
an internal acceptance. The astronomical polynomial is not a practical advantage.

This file governs the theorem. ASYMMETRIC_OPERATION, FRESH_SPANNERS and
RESOURCE_QUALIFICATION retain the derivation history. JOINT_RESTRICTIONS supplies
the improved support-safe cache, replacing normalized child queries in the
engineering prototype. No other scientific branch is modified or imported.

## 1. Input, output and the precise probability oracle

Let P,Q be distributions on [O]^T, O>=2, T>=1. At every cut the conditional
future distributions p_h=P(.|h), h in support(P), have linear span dimension at
most r>=1. The input consists of independent FULL P trajectories, conditional Q
samples at positive-Q prefixes, and next-token Q probability VALUE queries at
such prefixes. A value query returns a warranted interval at a requested number
of bits. Its actual computation cost, denoted C_Q(T,bits), is not free. Assume
D(P||Q)<=Delta<infinity, nats. No P conditional or likelihood oracle is supplied.
Q can have arbitrary predictive rank. There is no target spectral/positivity gap.

For accuracy epsilon and failure probability delta in(0,1/4), put
A=ceil[1000(r+O+T+1/delta)]. The proposed algorithm has polynomial numbers of P
samples, Q calls, stored bits and inference arithmetic operations in
A,1/epsilon. It asks polynomially many probability BITS; multiply each service
cost in. If that primitive is polynomial-time in these arguments, the entire
operation is polynomial-time. Conditional draws alone do not in general simulate
the precision required here with polynomially many samples.

With probability at least1-delta the finite returned autoregressive model obeys

    TV(P,P_hat) <= epsilon +128 A^3 Delta^(1/16384).       (1)

It retains no Q evaluator and makes ZERO Q calls during inference or sampling.
The right side can be vacuous at any realistic misspecification. Its significance
is a horizon-independent Holder exponent and a condition-free finite compiler,
if the proposed proof survives whole challenge. This does not assert an efficient
positive-HMM realization, practical forecasting, novelty or physical acquisition.

## 2. Ordinary geometric acquisition, separately at each cut

Fix a parameter0<tau<=1/(100A), write x=A/tau and d'=delta/(100T). Use the schedule

    C=8(r+1), b=tau/O, a=b/2, theta=tau/[4(r+1)],
    D=ceil(x^40), v=a tau, xi=tau,
    gamma0=d' tau/100,
    zeta=d' tau^2/[100 D(r+1)],
    N=ceil(x^60), M=ceil[(A N/zeta)^10],
    theta_geo=zeta/[100(r+1)N],
    eta=min{zeta/[100(r+1)], theta_geo d'/[100 N M]}.

At every nontrivial cut sample N fresh P trajectories. The sampled prefixes have
positive Q probability. Conditional chain rule and Pinsker give

    Pr_h(||p_h-q_h||_1>eta)<=2Delta/eta^2.

Thus all NT fresh queried rows are eta-close except with probability at most
2TNDelta/eta^2. No conditional closeness is asserted for their children.

There exists a subset of at most r sampled TRUE rows whose symmetric coefficient
parallelotope contains1-gamma0 of the P-prefix population. Indeed a maximum-volume
basis of all sampled true rows contains those samples with coefficients<=1. For
any fixed index subset I of size<=r, condition on its values. If its parallelotope
has population mass<1-gamma0, the other N-|I| samples all lie in it with probability
at most exp[-gamma0(N-r)]. Union over at most(r+1)N^r choices. This is an existence
witness, not a P query or computed basis.

To compute a basis, sample M features from
mu_geo=(U+sum_(i=1)^N q_(h_i))/(N+1), where U is the uniform future law. Put
u_i(j)=q_(h_i)(f_j)/(M mu_geo(f_j)). Unknown v_i formed with p_(h_i) have rank<=r.
On the good-row event, Markov plus a union bound gives

    |p_(h_i)(f_j)-q_(h_i)(f_j)|/mu_geo(f_j)<=theta_geo

at every queried pair, except with probability NM eta/theta_geo<=d'/100. Hence
||U-V||op<=sqrt(N/M)theta_geo. Retain singular directions above a threshold between
2 and4 times this known perturbation and compute a2-barycentric column spanner
there. At most r columns remain. Each original column has an l1 sketch residual
at most4(1+2r)sqrt(N)theta_geo<zeta/10 against these selected columns, coefficients
bounded by2. A small threshold gap and approximate SVD/volume swaps suffice:
no singular value of the UNKNOWN P basis is inverted. The retained-coordinate
condition is bounded by the known truncation threshold and therefore costs only
its logarithm in ordinary bit arithmetic. Geometry cache errors occupy fixed
slack inside these constants; see JOINT_RESTRICTIONS.

Independently of any selected coefficients, a finite net for [-4,4]^N and
Hoeffding preserve the full L1 norm of EVERY teacher-row combination to zeta/10.
Consequently each sampled q_i is within zeta/2 of a combination of the selected
Q rows. Combine with the hidden true population spanner: outside gamma0 P-mass,
p_h is within r zeta of a combination of selected q's, coefficients<=2r. Its
mass differs from1 by at most r zeta. Normalize its coefficients by that mass:
the resulting signed density z0 has mass1, coefficients<=3r and

    ||p_h-z0||_1<=4r zeta.                            (2)

All selected rows are FRESH Q conditionals. Neither previous-basis children nor
their teacher error enter the selection or its importance measure.

## 3. Fresh features, positivity in measure and feasible proxies

Append a uniform row to the selected rows, R_1,...,R_S, S<=r+1, and set
mu=sum R_i/S. Then R_i/mu<=S and mu>=1/(S O^L), L remaining length. Draw D NEW
features from mu, independently after all basis choices. Coefficients satisfy
sum alpha=1, |alpha_i|<=C and finite-feature density z_alpha/mu>=tau. Uniform
coefficients are strictly feasible. At finite precision the implemented threshold
is2tau with slack, while the following statements concern exact virtual rows.

The full negative mass of every feasible state is at most v, simultaneously over
ALL possible inference choices. To see this, apply uniform Hoeffding/net bounds
to (-sum alpha_i R_i/mu)_+. Its empirical negative mass is0, its envelope<=SC,
and its coefficient sup-norm Lipschitz constant<=S^2. The sample count D pays
uniform error v (with half reserved for arithmetic). This is a negative-MASS
bound, not global pointwise positivity inferred from finitely many tests.

Pad the proxy (2) towards mu with weight4tau. It has mass1, coefficients<C and
L1 error e<=4r zeta+8tau<=9tau. If the unpadded density is>=-tau mu at a feature,
the padded density is>=3tau mu. Violating that condition has mu-probability at
most4r zeta/tau. Conditional on all acquired geometry, the expected P-prefix mass
without a feature-feasible proxy is at most gamma0+4D r zeta/tau<=d'tau/20.
Markov over the fresh features gives bad P-prefix mass<=tau except with
probability d'/20. This is P-weighted coverage of ACTUAL histories. It never
conditions on a previously selected basis prefix, avoiding the failed bias step.

## 4. Arbitrary child restrictions enter only a clipped logarithm

At the next cut cache V_(i,o)(f)=R_i(o,f), evaluated on that cut's features.
Each V is a subprobability density<=1. For a current state alpha and actual token
probability pi_o>=a, its reference is w_o=sum alpha_i V_(i,o)/pi_o. No normalized
Q(.|h_i o) query is needed. Bounds below allow every such child without any rank,
target-closeness or coverage promise. Its coefficient box is C/a.

Use delta_L=theta a^L and [z]_L=max(z,delta_L). The floor's total added mass is
at most theta. Every feasible state has excess k_z=int([z]_L-z)<=v+theta.
Let K=(r+1)C/a+2 and B=log[K/(theta a^T)]. Clipped densities lie between delta_L
and K, their pairwise log ratios have magnitude<=B, and their total clipped
masses are at most K.

Uniformly over bounded alpha0,alpha,beta, the function

    ((z_alpha0-z_alpha)/mu) log([z_alpha]_L/[w_beta]_L)

has envelope2SCB and coefficient sup-norm Lipschitz constant at most
2S^2 B+2SC(S+k)/delta_L, k<=r+1 for each token. A coefficient net followed by
Hoeffding therefore integrates it to error xi. Although the floor is exponentially
small in T, ONLY the logarithm of that Lipschitz constant enters the sample
count. No child-dominating importance measure is required. The features remain
independent of all bases; uniformity covers adaptive future coefficient choices.

For the current raw reference w, minimize the finite convex objective

    J(alpha)=D^-1 sum_j [z_alpha(f_j)/mu(f_j)
                         *log(z_alpha(f_j)/[w]_L(f_j))
                         -z_alpha(f_j)/mu(f_j)] .     (3)

Its first-order residual is at most xi. The minus-linear term is necessary
because normalization is in the FULL space, not the empirical feature sum.
Uniform integration gives int(z0-z)log([z]_L/[w]_L)>=-2xi. For a true p and a
feasible proxy z0 with ||p-z0||1<=e, put
Phi_L(p,z)=int p log(p/[z]_L), Z_w=int[w]_L. Then

    Phi_L(p,z)<=Phi_L(p,w)+log Z_w+2xi+B(e+2k_z).      (4)

Proof: insert z0, costing eB, and use the first-order inequality. Replacing z
by [z]_L costs Bk_z. Log-sum gives int[z]_L log([w]_L/[z]_L)
<=(1+k_z)log(Z_w/(1+k_z)). Subtracting log Z_w leaves at most Bk_z since
Z_w<=K. This establishes (4) without a pointwise-positive full signed state.

At bad histories, Phi_L(p,z)-Phi_L(p,w)<=B directly from the clipped log bound.

## 5. Exact transition normalization retains token KL

At a state of exact mass1 and negative mass<=v, let m_o=int z(o,f). Output

    pi_o=max(m_o,b)/M0, M0=sum_o max(m_o,b).

Here1<=M0<=1+v+O b<=2 and pi_o>=a. The raw child is w_o=z(o,.)/pi_o. As
pi_o delta_(L-1)>=delta_L, the exact unnormalized chain rule gives

    sum_o p(o)Phi_(L-1)(p(.|o),w_o)
       <=Phi_L(p,z)-D(p_tokens||pi).                 (5)

The child normalization is uniformly near1, independent of its coverage:

    Z_wo<=m_o/pi_o+v/pi_o+theta
          <=1+v+O b+v/a+theta,
    log Z_wo<=v+O b+v/a+theta<=4tau.                 (6)

The last direct bound is essential: a different Jensen normalization bound can
cancel the token KL and would not prove a compiler. Every projection resets the
parent negative mass to v, so v/a=tau never recurses through T. Token cache
rounding changes (6) by the explicit small terms in JOINT_RESTRICTIONS; (5)
holds for any actual positive pi and remains EXACT for that actual token rule.

Initialize with (1-tau)Q+tau U, whose Phi<=Delta+2tau and negative mass0. Its
required marginal/joint feature data are also cached. At the empty future the
only state is1 and Phi=0. Apply (4)-(6), average under the FIXED P prefix law,
and sum over cuts. The good-proxy error<=9tau, bad mass<=tau and floor/negative
errors give

    D(P||P_hat)<=Delta+2tau+T[6tau+12B tau].          (7)

The sum of token KLs is the KL of the ENTIRE output law by chain rule. There is
no selected-child coverage, P conditional oracle, inverse target-state matrix,
or recursively worsened teacher error in (7). With finite arithmetic, value-
oracle error, known Slater slack and convex-solve residual reserves, use

    D(P||P_hat)<=Delta+40T(B+1)tau.                  (8)

## 6. Explicit resource domination

For x>=1000 the schedule has d'>=x^-2, tau>=x^-1, a>=x^-1 and theta>=x^-1;
A,r+1,O,T,C<=x. It follows successively that D<=x^41, zeta>=x^-50,
N<=x^61, M<=x^1200, theta_geo>=x^-112 and eta>=x^-1400. Therefore
Delta<=x^-4096 makes the good-row failure at most2x^-1234, well inside delta.
The exact bound NM eta/theta_geo<=d'/100 pays the pointwise geometry error.

For sample-compression, gamma0>=x^-4 gives gamma0(N-r)>=x^56/2, while
log[(r+1)N^r/(d'/100)]<=x^3. Thus N pays its failure probability. For the full
L1 sketch a coefficient net gives a bound below10^9 N^7 zeta^-3 (including
confidence); (A N/zeta)^10 dominates it since A>=1000 and N>=1,zeta<=1.

For the gradient sketch use B<=A log x<=x^2, envelope<=x^5, parameter dimension
<=x^2, net log per coordinate<=x^2 and confidence log<=x. With half tolerances
and fixed constants the sufficient Hoeffding bound is below x^24. The negative-
mass bound has a smaller majorant because1/v<=x^2. D=ceil(x^40) pays both, and
the additional token/cut union only changes their confidence log. Across all
events the allocated failure is less than delta, including finite conditional-
sample implementation failures.

Geometry is computed at polynomial BIT accuracy around a known truncation
threshold. Inference (3) has bounded gradient and Hessian polynomial in S,B,1/tau;
the rational coefficient polytope has a known uniform Slater point. A linear-
minimization/Frank--Wolfe procedure decreases its bounded objective by a polynomial
multiple of the squared first-order gap. Ordinary rational LPs and warranted log
intervals therefore produce gap<=tau in polynomial time. No installed SVD or
CLARABEL run is presumed to certify these worst-case statements.

Each full row/joint density evaluation uses at most T next-token calls. The
compilation count is bounded by a fixed polynomial, for example a constant
multiple of T^2[NM+(O+1)(r+1)D+M+D], plus geometric/convex arithmetic. The output
stores O[T O(r+1)D] density/marginal scalars and feature strings. Their bit lengths
are polynomial in T log(O/a),logN,logM,logD,log(1/tau). During inference only
these finite arrays, a bounded rational coefficient vector and convex programs
are used. There is no hidden Q call. Its service cost is nevertheless fully paid
at compilation; probability VALUES, not sample-only access, are load-bearing.

## 7. Choose tau and derive the stated error

Take dyadic tau_acc between (epsilon/(1024A^2))^4 and twice that value. For Delta>0
take dyadic tau_noise between A Delta^(1/4096) and twice that value; for Delta0
take0. Let tau=max(tau_acc,tau_noise). Rational power comparisons suffice. If
tau>1/(100A), return uniform independent tokens. In this case the right side
of(1) exceeds1: tau_acc cannot cause it, so
Delta^(1/16384)>(1/(200A^2))^(1/4).

Otherwise Delta<=(tau/A)^4096 and all resource gates above apply. Since
B<=A log(A/tau), (8) and Pinsker imply the conservative bound

    TV(P,P_hat)<=sqrt(Delta/2)+10A^2 tau^(1/4).

Use tau^(1/4)<=tau_acc^(1/4)+tau_noise^(1/4) to obtain(1), with room for its
constants. Tau>=tau_acc bounds ALL sample counts and sizes by a fixed polynomial
in A,1/epsilon, regardless of how tiny Delta is. T does not appear in the
exponents of epsilon or Delta. No claim of useful moderate-Delta constants follows.

## 8. Source, execution and unsolved qualifications

Liu--Moitra2411.07536v1, §§3,5,6,7 is the strongest consumed constructive source:
same-target conditional queries, bounded barycentric geometry, density-mixture
sketches, robust truncation and KL convex inference are established machinery.
The new proposed interface is fresh-P acquisition under global KL to a different
arbitrary-rank teacher, coupled to signed full states and the asymmetric clipped-
log telescope. A same-target learner cannot be transferred merely by renaming Q.
Historical priority of this particular extension has not been established.

The retained T8 engineering run uses MUCH smaller budgets and floating tools.
It checks access separation and finite caching, not(1). The rank2 target/rank16
teacher diagnostic, all output probabilities, counts, first failed implementation,
corrected run and ordinary two-component EM comparison remain visible. The EM
model has narrower structural knowledge and no Q calls; it was dramatically
faster. No best-incumbent computational advantage is asserted. The proof itself
remains PROPOSED pending independent whole challenge.

# Joint restrictions and literal finite-precision access

30 October 2026. This strengthens/simplifies the proposed compiler's access
implementation. It replaces the normalized-child cache in the engineering
prototype and the support-cutoff construction in RESOURCE_QUALIFICATION §4.
The existing execution is preserved; this note does not claim a second run.

## 1. Do not divide a teacher child

For a selected positive-Q prefix h_i, store at the next cut's feature f_j the
JOINT restriction

    V_(i,o)(f_j) = Q(o f_j | h_i).

For the uniform row the value is O^(-L), where L is the parent's remaining
length. Each V_(i,o) is a subprobability density on child futures, bounded by1.
Its mass is the separately stored q_i(o). Its value is a product of next-token
probabilities starting at h_i. It never requires a query at h_i o.

Given parent coefficients alpha and the ACTUALLY OUTPUT token probability pi_o,
the reference array is

    w_o(f_j) = sum_i alpha_i V_(i,o)(f_j) / pi_o.

This is exactly the restriction of the virtual full signed parent density,
divided by pi_o. Coefficients are bounded by C/a. The asymmetric gradient lemma
uses only 0<=V_i<=1, integral V_i<=1 and a bounded coefficient box; it therefore
holds unchanged. No child is sampled, placed into the importance mixture, or
required to approximate a target conditional law. If q_i(o)=0 its entire joint
restriction is zero. No zero-probability conditional oracle is needed.

## 2. A full-future probability at finite precision

At a positive-Q prefix h the product for a fixed continuation f has factors in
[0,1]. Request each next-token factor to absolute accuracy eps/(8T). Track an
outward interval for the partial product. Before querying an extension, either
its partial product has certified positive lower endpoint, or its upper endpoint
is at most eps/2. In the latter case return0: the final product is at most eps/2.
If neither condition holds, refine the current factor. A value that stays
unresolved within the requested factor precision forces the partial product to
be at most eps/2 after adjusting the constants. Thus the algorithm does not need
to decide whether an arbitrary tiny probability is exactly zero.

A more literal fixed-budget implementation uses next-token intervals of width
eps/(16T) from the start: if an extension's lower endpoint is nonpositive, its
upper probability is at most eps/(8T), so STOP rather than query it. Its final
product is then at most eps/(8T). Otherwise the extension is certified positive.
Products of all non-stopped factors have error at most the sum of widths. All
teacher queries are at known positive-Q prefixes. Every sampled raw basis prefix
is positive-Q because P(h)>0 and D(P||Q)<infinity. This is a consequence of the
supplied promise, not a test by the learner.

Both V_(i,o) and the fresh full-row densities can therefore be cached to arbitrary
absolute eps using polynomially many queries and O(log(T/eps)) probability bits.
This is a VALUE-ORACLE result. Its service cost must be charged at that precision.
It is NOT a polynomial conditional-SAMPLE-only simulation: estimating an
exponentially small absolute tolerance from draws can take exponentially many.

## 3. Robust cache, constraints and the real transition

Let eps be a uniform absolute error bound for every cached row density, joint
restriction and token probability. Normalize the token rows as rational
probability vectors with l1 error<=2O eps. Put E_m=2S C O eps. Then the actual
computed marginals mhat have sum1 and satisfy |mhat_o-m_o|<=E_m. The actual token
rule uses max(mhat_o,b), normalized. Its denominator is at most

    1+v+O b+O E_m,

since the true signed token marginals have negative mass at most v. If the
displayed excess is<=1, every actual pi_o>=b/2=a. Moreover the TRUE virtual
reference normalization satisfies

    integral max(z(o,.)/pi_o,delta_child)
       <=1+v+O b+O E_m+E_m/a+v/a+theta_floor.

This is the only place token-row rounding changes the transition normalization
proof. The exact chain-rule inequality holds for ANY actual positive pi, hence
has no additional approximation term. There is no sequence of inferred teacher
conditional-error divisions.

For mixture floor mu_min=1/(S O^L), the true feature ratios R_i/mu are at most S.
Store rational approximations rhat_i and define muhat=sum_i rhat_i/S EXACTLY.
For eps<=mu_min/4 the ratio error is at most 4S eps/mu_min per row. Thus all
coefficient-state feature values differ from their true values by at most
4S^2 C eps/mu_min. Impose the rational constraint zhat/muhat>=2tau. The true
padded proxy is>=3tau at good features and the true values of all feasible
states are>=tau when the last error is<=tau/2. The uniform coefficient vector
is strictly feasible with ratio exactly1. Sum alpha=1 is imposed exactly, so
the virtual full signed density has mass exactly1 regardless of rounding.

At child features the raw reference value has error at most S C eps/a.
Clipping and log are Lipschitz with constants1 and1/delta_min. The empirical
gradient discrepancy is bounded by a polynomial in S,C,1/a,1/mu_min,
1/delta_min,B times eps. Choose eps so that this bound, O E_m+E_m/a, and all
ratio errors use at most tau/100 each. For example a sufficiently conservative
single value is

    eps = [tau a delta_min mu_min /
           (10^6 (S+1)(C+1)(O+1)(T+1)(B+1))]^4.

One may replace B by the explicit rational integer upper bound A*ceil(log2 x)
times2, avoiding a transcendental request in the accuracy rule. Finite interval
evaluation/LP certificates pay the same remaining tolerance. The bit length is
polynomial in T,log O,log(1/tau),log D,log N,log M. The tiny VALUE of eps is not
a polynomial-in-1/eps query-count claim: the primitive supplies requested
probability BITS, whose actual service cost is explicitly multiplied in.

Geometry has its own preliminary tolerance. With
mu_geo_min=1/((N+1)O^L), request density error at most
theta_geo*mu_geo_min/[1000(N+1)]. This changes the ratio columns by at most
theta_geo/100, fitting inside the robust-SVD constants in FRESH_SPANNERS. Its
bit length is again polynomial. It is not omitted from the value-oracle bill.

## 4. Sampling features and output tokens

Conditional Q-sampling is already an input primitive. If instead it is implemented
from next-token probability queries, draw a persistent uniform and compare it
with the categorical cumulative sums using successively refined intervals. An
exact chosen token has positive Q probability almost surely, so every subsequent
conditional call is valid. The probability that a comparison remains unresolved
at b bits is at most 2O*2^-b. Across a prescribed polynomial number of calls,
truncate at a known polynomial bit budget and count any unresolved outcome as
a declared compilation failure. A union bound fits this inside delta/10.
This avoids silently sampling an impossible prefix by rounding a zero upward.

The returned finite model uses rational token probabilities and no Q reference.
They can be sampled with expected polynomial fair-bit work, or with a finite bit
budget and separately allocated TV error. The teaching oracle's own numerical
complexity and the full-trajectory source's acquisition cost are inputs, not free
physical measurement capabilities.

## 5. Status

These are mathematical access/perturbation statements for the general proposed
compiler. The finite engineering run used normalized child arrays, floating SVD
and CLARABEL, with a full-support teacher, and hence did not exercise support-zero
or formal interval branches. Its output is not a verified implementation of the
formal astronomical resource schedule. The proof still awaits independent whole
challenge; no practical advantage or installed-library worst-case complexity is
claimed.

P is a law on O^T with predictive linear rank<=r at every cut. The learner receives
iid FULL P trajectories; next-token probability/conditional-sample access is only
to a fixed arbitrary-rank Q, with the supplied promise D(P||Q)<=Delta. Accuracy
epsilon and failure probability delta are in(0,1/4). Rank is not a positive-HMM
realization or a singular-value lower bound. Q is not copied into the output.

Let A=ceil[1000(r+O+T+1/delta)]. Subject to the full proof below, the proposed
algorithm has polynomial sample/query/representation/inference complexity in
r,O,T,1/epsilon,1/delta and returns a teacher-free sequential model with

    TV(P,P_hat)<=epsilon+128 A^3 Delta^(1/16384).        (1)

The bound is deliberately weak. Probability values are requested at a polynomial
number of bits; their ACTUAL oracle computation costs must be multiplied in.
No paid-compute, physical or practical predictive advantage follows. A and all
exponents are explicit, independent of r,T. Confidence dependence is polynomial
in1/delta, not claimed logarithmic. The model may solve convex programs per token.

## 2. Parameter choice

Take a dyadic tau_acc between (epsilon/(1024A^2))^4 and twice that value. If Delta>0,
take dyadic tau_noise between A Delta^(1/4096) and twice that value, using rational
power comparisons; for Delta0 take tau_noise0. Put tau=max(tau_acc,tau_noise).
If tau>1/(100A), output uniform independent tokens. The claimed bound then exceeds1
by the calculation in Section6, so this branch is not a hidden learning claim.
Otherwise set the exact rational parameters and explicit sample counts in
FRESH_SPANNERS Section5. In particular Delta<=(tau/A)^4096 holds.

At each cut obtain <=r fresh teacher rows by that acquisition. Append the
uniform-future row. No parent/child is inserted into the spanner candidate set.
Independently draw D fresh projection futures from this basis mixture mu.
Store the basis probabilities on those features, normalized by mu, and the next-
token probabilities at every basis prefix. For every earlier-cut basis row and
symbol, EVALUATE its child future density on the next cut's fresh features and
cache these values as well. The uniform row's restriction is known exactly.
These arrays are finite and of polynomial total size. No child samples or
P-conditional future samples are used. Source sections3/6/7 of Liu--Moitra provide
the ordinary spanner/convex-inference machinery but not this misspecification transfer.

## 3. The compiled generator

Maintain coefficients alpha over the fresh rows plus uniform, with sum alpha1
and |alpha_i|<=C=8(r+1). Initially use (1-tau)Q+tau U. All its needed first-step
and child-feature data are cached at compilation. At each token:

1. Compute raw next-token marginals m_o from alpha and the cached next-token rows.
2. Sample p_hat(o)=max(m_o,b)/sum max(m_o,b), b=tau/O. It is a valid strictly
   positive categorical law with each entry>=a=b/2 on every possible history.
3. Restrict/renormalize the current signed state with beta_i=alpha_i q_i(o)/p_hat(o).
4. Using only the cached next-cut child values, minimize the convex empirical
   generalized KL in ASYMMETRIC_OPERATION(1) over new fresh-row coefficients:
   sum alpha1, |alpha|<=C, and z_alpha(f_j)/mu(f_j)>=tau.
5. Use the minimizer as the next coefficient state. At the empty future take the
   trivial scalar state1. No teacher callback is retained by the generator.

Uniform coefficients1/S always give a strictly feasible point. The gradient and
Hessian on this domain have polynomial bounds: z/mu>=tau, R_i/mu<=S and logs
bounded by B. A conditional-gradient method with linear-program subproblems can
stop at a certified Frank--Wolfe gap<=tau; it is not a free nonconvex/global-fit
oracle. All arrays and coefficient limits are known at inference.

## 4. What the acquired events give

FRESH_SPANNERS plus RESOURCE_QUALIFICATION pay, with total failure<delta:

* At every cut the fresh teacher rows approximate all but tau P-mass of actual
  target conditional futures by feature-feasible signed states of mass1, coefficient
  bound C, and L1 error e<=9tau. This is P-weighted, not uniform conditional closeness.
* Every state feasible for a cut's finite program has negative FULL-density
  mass<=v=a tau. It need not be pointwise positive away from the features.
* Uniform asymmetric-gradient integration error<=tau holds for ALL candidate,
  comparison and arbitrary-child coefficient states in their bounded boxes.
  Thus data-dependent projection choices and adaptive generated histories are covered.

The feature-positive proxy premise is obtained with a Markov bound under the
FIXED P prefix law, independently of the projection features. The KL analysis
also averages under that law. It does not condition on a prefix selected by the
previous basis, which was the failed fresh-only argument.

## 5. Full sequence error, not only a local module

Use delta_L=theta_floor a^L, theta_floor=tau/[4(r+1)], and define the unnormalized
potential Phi_L(p,z)=sum p log[p/max(z,delta_L)]. Initialization satisfies
Phi_T<=Delta-log(1-tau)<=Delta+2tau. At the terminal empty future it is0.

The exact transition identity in ASYMMETRIC_OPERATION(4) retains the NEGATIVE
token KL. Projection adds log Z_w plus bounded approximation/sketch terms.
Importantly log Z_w<=v+O b+v/a+theta_floor<=4tau UNIFORMLY, rather than using an
upper bound that cancels the token KL. Therefore the exact-data receiver gives

    D(P||P_hat)<=Delta+2tau+T[6tau+12 B tau].          (2)

Bad histories add at most B times their P-mass, already included here. The KL
chain rule on the actual strictly positive compiled token conditionals identifies
the sum of token KLs with D(P||P_hat). This completes the SEQUENTIAL propagation:
there is no recursively worsened teacher error, state inverse or unqualified
child coverage left in(2). With paid oracle/arithmetic/optimization precision
reserve, the conservative version is

    D(P||P_hat)<=Delta+40T(B+1)tau.                   (3)

The rounding/normalization and signed negative-mass bills are explicit terms;
they are not called a generic contraction. B may be chosen globally as

    B=log[(S_max C/a+2)/(theta_floor a^T)], S_max=r+1.

## 6. From(3) to the stated Hölder form

For A>=1000, tau<=1/(100A), the displayed expression satisfies
B<=A log(A/tau). Hence40T(B+1)tau<=160 A^3 sqrt(tau), using
tau log(A/tau)<=2A sqrt(tau). Pinsker yields

    TV(P,P_hat)<=sqrt(Delta/2)+10 A^2 tau^(1/4).

The dyadic choice of tau gives(1) with room in its constants. If the uniform
fallback branch is taken, tau_noise>1/(100A) (tau_acc cannot cause it), so
Delta^(1/16384)>(1/(200A^2))^(1/4);128A^3 times this is>=1. The fallback is thus
correct at the stated, possibly vacuous, error bound. As Delta->0 the guarantee
is nonvacuous, but the exponent makes its practical noise tolerance very poor.

Because tau>=tau_acc, the largest resource count is bounded by a fixed polynomial
in A and1/epsilon, independently of how tiny Delta is. T appears in the polynomial
and log floor, NEVER in the exponent of Delta or epsilon. This is the intended
condition-free form. Explicit finite-precision and source-operation handling are
separate below; unverified runtime of a numerical package is not part of the claim.

## 7. Actual execution versus theorem state

At this writing the GENERAL derivation is proposed and awaits independent whole
challenge. It is not validated by a successful small optimization or a data hash.
The formal polynomial budgets are enormous and are not a practical sampler claim.
An executable resource/inequality receiver and a teacher-call-gated engineering
compiler are the next discriminating work, without confusing their diagnostics
with proof of(1). Ordinary spectral/TT/conditional learners retain their actual
resources; no numerical advantage over a strong fitted model is asserted.

# Resource and finite-precision qualification for the proposed compiler

This closes the parameter interfaces in the proposed proof; independent whole
review is pending. None of the formal budgets is advertised as practical.

## 1. One polynomial, not a recursion in the horizon

Use A,x,tau,d',D,gamma0,zeta,N,M,theta_geo,eta exactly as in FRESH_SPANNERS5.
Every cut uses the SAME bounds. For A>=1000 and0<tau<=1/(100A):

    d'>=x^-2, zeta>=x^-50, gamma0>=x^-4,
    N<=x^61, M<=x^1200, theta_geo>=x^-112,
    eta>=x^-1400.                                    (1)

Here D<=x^41 since ceil(x^40)<=2x^40<=x^41. Also100(r+1)<=A and
100T<=A, and tau>=x^-1. These inequalities immediately give zeta>=x^-46;
the weaker x^-50 leaves room. A N/zeta<=x^112 implies M<=x^1121<=x^1200.
Then theta_geo>=x^-112 and the second term of eta is at least x^-1376.
The first term is at least x^-51. This proves(1).

N also pays the population sample-compression event: r/gamma0<=x^5 and
log(1/d')<=2log x, so the predecessor's already generous
(r/gamma0)^10 log(1/d') is below x^60. Alternatively substitute into the explicit
union bound(r+1)N^r exp[-gamma0(N-r)]; the negative exponent dominates because
gamma0(N-r)>=x^56/2 whereas its logarithmic competitor is at most O(x^2).

M=(A N/zeta)^10 dominates the full-L1 row-sketch Hoeffding/net bound. For coefficient
boxes[-4,4]^N the envelope is<=8N² and the sup-norm Lipschitz constant<=2N².
A zeta/(100N²) net has logarithm<=N log(1+800N²/zeta). The needed sample count
is bounded by a constant times N^7 zeta^-3 plus the confidence term; the stated
power10 exceeds it because A>=1000. Uniform row proximity in the sketch fails
with probability<=N M eta/theta_geo<=d'/100.

The global teacher event fails with probability<=2 T N Delta/eta². If
Delta<=x^-4096, (1) bounds this by2x^-1235 (or a still smaller bound), below the
allocated confidence. Equivalently it is much stronger than the explicit
d'eta²/(100TN) condition. No term tau^-T enters this probability calculation.

## 2. D pays the asymmetric projection events

The full density floor is delta_L=theta_floor a^L, theta_floor=tau/[4(r+1)]
and a=tau/(2O). Let K=(r+1)C/a+2. On all cuts

    B=log(K/(theta_floor a^T))<=A log x.

A coefficient sup-net for the clipped-gradient class has dimension at most
2(r+1)+O(r+1), if all child families are included together. The larger family
only adds a polynomial factor; it does not need a child sampling measure. Its
envelope is2S C B. The Lipschitz constant contains1/delta_L, but only its LOG
appears in the net size. Since T<=A, that log is O(A log x). The Hoeffding/net
sample bound is conservatively below x^24, including confidence and constant
factors; D=ceil(x^40) exceeds it.

For negative mass, the envelope is S C and coefficient Lipschitz constant S².
The desired error v=a tau has inverse<=x^4. Its analogous sample bound is below
x^24 too. Use half the allotted errors for the exact-data concentration and leave
the remaining halves for arithmetic. Multiplying these bounds by fixed constants
still lies below x^40 at x>=1000.

For feature-positive proxies, Section3 of FRESH_SPANNERS gives expected bad
P-prefix mass<=gamma0+4D r zeta/tau<=d'tau/20. Markov therefore bounds the chance
that its actual bad mass exceeds tau by d'/20. This is conditional on the acquired
basis, with a NEW independent feature sample. Across cuts and the other events,
the failure budget is below delta. Generated-history dependence is covered by
uniform coefficient events; it is not an additional union over exponentially
many prefixes.

## 3. No spectral conditioning oracle

In geometry, the unknown true-row sketch has rank<=r and the computed sketch is
within the stated known norm perturbation. Singular values above twice that
perturbation can be retained; those below can be discarded at paid L1 error.
If a singular value lies on a proposed threshold, choose a threshold gap among
r+1 levels between2 and4 times the perturbation, at spacing polynomially small
relative to it. Approximate SVD to that precision identifies a valid gap. The
smallest retained singular value then has a KNOWN lower bound. Pivot construction
and volume-doubling take polynomially many steps in its logarithm. Relaxing the
swap/stop thresholds by fixed factors pays finite arithmetic without deciding
equality of unknown real singular values. Constants in zeta/100 leave this room.

This is ordinary robust-spanner machinery with its actual hypotheses supplied;
it is not a new exact-rank oracle or free inverse of a target singular value.

## 4. Probability precision and teacher support

Every sketch measure includes a uniform future, so its density is at least
1/((N+1)O^L) in geometry and1/((r+1)O^L) in projection. Thus cached ratios can be
evaluated to any required accuracy with an absolute probability request having
only O(L log O) additional bits. Products of next-token probabilities have
absolute error bounded by the sum of their individual errors.

All raw basis prefixes are P-sampled and have positive Q probability when Delta
is finite. If the Q interface only supports positive-probability histories,
there is still no need for a zero-prefix query: child rows with next probability
below c_cut are replaced by the known uniform conditional, retaining their next
token mass. Heavy children have a certified positive probability and may be
queried. Choose c_cut<=tau a delta_min/[1000 S C O], where
delta_min=theta_floor a^T. The resulting full restriction error is at most
2S C O c_cut; after division by p_hat>=a and clipping the log its effect is at
most O(S C O c_cut/(a delta_min))<=tau/100. This is a precision bill, not a
division of conditional teacher error at each depth.

A queried future product can stop before an unsupported extension once its
partial product is below its required absolute tolerance. Otherwise refinement
certifies a positive partial product before requesting the next conditional.
At a true zero, the former event settles at the known tolerance; at a value above
tolerance, the latter settles. Only polynomially many precision bits are needed.
No unacquired total conditional P oracle or Q sample from an impossible history
is thereby granted.

Finite conditional-sampling accuracy, if the primitive is not exact, is allocated
across the known polynomial number of feature draws by coupling/union bound. Its
requested error and ACTUAL service cost must be charged. It is not automatically
obtained from a pointwise probability response at no computational cost.

## 5. Finite cached arrays and convex inference

Take all density/marginal cache errors small enough that their propagated error
through division by the known mixture floors and clipped logs is<=tau/100 per
step. A sufficient accuracy is a fixed polynomial in tau,a,delta_min, the mixture
floor,1/D,1/N,1/M and1/(S C O T). Its BIT LENGTH is polynomial in
T log(O/a), log(1/tau),logN,logM,logD. Absolute errors may be exponentially small
in T; their bit requirement is not exponential in T.

Store normalized rational next-token rows, so their row sums are exactly1.
Their discrepancy from the underlying teacher rows is included in the preceding
restriction/log budget. Use empirical feature lower constraint2tau with arithmetic
slack: the true padded proxy is>=3tau, while every accepted coefficient state has
true feature density>=tau. Uniform coefficients give empirical value1 and known
Slater slack. Coefficient sums are imposed exactly; the virtual full density's
mass is therefore1 even when off-feature entries are signed.

The empirical generalized-KL objective's Hessian is bounded by a polynomial in
S and1/tau, and its gradient by a polynomial in S,B. Linear minimization over
the rational coefficient polytope is an ordinary polynomial-size LP. Short-step
Frank--Wolfe decreases the objective by at least a polynomial multiple of the
squared dual gap; its bounded objective range therefore permits a polynomial
iteration bound to a certified first-order gap<=tau. Log evaluations at paid
precision and a conservative gap tolerance suffice. This is a constructive
convex inference operation, not an unspecified nonlinear global-fit oracle.

The model stores only the finite feature strings/arrays, next-token rows,
parameters and inference algorithm. The full teacher row densities in the proof
are virtual mathematical witnesses, NEVER post-compilation evaluation resources.
Rational categorical token probabilities can be sampled exactly in finite expected
bit time, or with a bounded randomness budget and a separately allocated TV error.

## 6. Current status

These are detailed derivations of the access/precision/resource gates, not a claim
that an installed SVD/convex package has been validated at the formal astronomical
sample schedule. Root/peer whole challenge is still needed before accepting the
proposed full theorem. Practical compiler implementation, usefulness at moderate
Delta, and advantage against the best equally informed conventional learner remain
separate. No physical/native world-model acquisition is claimed.

# Why a local large-memory fluctuation construction does not replace the full law

30 October 2026. Root consequence of the complementary elastic-counter
architecture. It uses only its pathwise physical-current relation and capacity,
not a guessed equilibration time or a limiting Gaussian calculation.

Let x be the real harmonic density field, J the complete signed bond current,
and z the actual per-bond elastic counters. The supplied local architecture
obeys, including any reflecting-boundary forces,

    dx=B dJ,   dz=dJ,   |z_i|<=b_N,
    (B j)_i=j_(i-1)-j_i.                                (1)

Thus x-Bz is an exact conserved vector. This is stronger than the total-counter
premise in the general locality theorem; the following conclusion applies to
this per-bond architecture and is not asserted for every local controller.

Set k=2pi/N, d=exp(ik)-1, and define the macroscopic fundamental density mode

    xi_N(t)=N^-1 sum_i exp(iki)x_i(t).

Exact continuity gives, on every path and at every actual time,

    xi_N(t)-xi_N(0)
      =(d/N)sum_i exp(iki)[z_i(t)-z_i(0)],
    |xi_N(t)-xi_N(0)|<=2b_N|d|<=4pi b_N/N.              (2)

For b_N=sqrt(N)(log N)^2, the bound tends to zero uniformly over all time,
although the corresponding fluctuation-mode allowance
sqrt(N)|xi_N(t)-xi_N(0)|<=4pi(log N)^2 diverges. There is consequently no conflict
between ordinary order-one Gaussian fluctuation evolution and a frozen
macroscopic density Fourier mode.

This separates three precision objectives:

| Objective | Consequence of this architecture |
|---|---|
| Stationary one-time visible law | May be exactly the supplied Gaussian marginal |
| Typical density fluctuation paths on N^2 time | May approach the ordinary OU path law when the prepared memory susceptibility grows |
| Order-one density-profile relaxation or complete speed-N history law | Cannot agree with ordinary heat relaxation for b_N=o(N), by (2) |

For example, an actual initial profile with a nonzero order-one fundamental
mode retains that mode up to o(1) for all times. The ordinary harmonic heat
bath changes it by a fixed fraction on physical N^2T. Even with stationary
Gaussian initialization, an event requiring an order-one change between two
specified macroscopic density modes becomes impossible for sufficiently large
N, while the ordinary Gaussian bath assigns a finite rare-history cost.
The one-time marginals can still agree because the controlled process mixes
over conserved initial x-Bz sectors.

The alternative is therefore useful for an explicitly finite-tolerance,
stationary fluctuation objective. It genuinely changes the architecture by
paying growing local capacity and prepared long-wavelength memory correlation.
It does not implement the full exclusion action or replace the shared-bit
construction's nonflat heat receiver. Conversely, the latter is not automatically
preferable when only ordinary typical observables are required. This comparison
must be made at the intended precision and actual initial-law interface.

# Native events suffice: a second corrector removes the external shared clock

30 October 2026. Root sustained follow-on construction. This is an addendum to
the reviewed positive-clock action files, which remain unchanged. Its consequence
is operational: the shared bit need not receive an externally timed reset.
It still must be updated atomically by every selected native event and coupled
to every selected port. Global interaction cost does not disappear.

## 1. The remaining zero-clock problem

Use fixed 0<=alpha<1 and the clean native ring rates r_i=c(1+alpha u delta_i),
where each native swap flips u. Set the external shared-clock rate to zero.
For F_H=A_H/A, the first corrector leaves u L_native F_H. The accepted quotient
estimate splits this into c u L_ex F_H+c alpha D F_H. The second term is bounded
by C_H/A and its time integral is superexponentially negligible. The unresolved
term was u g_H with

    g_H=L_ex F_H,  L_ex=sum_i(T_i-I).                       (1)

The inverse-activity theorem itself already holds with zero external clock.
The goal is to turn u g_H into an actual-generator coboundary plus an inverse-
activity remainder, without any hypothetical extra operation.

## 2. The missing finite-difference estimate

For every active exchange i,

    |g_H|<=8||H||_infinity,
    |Delta_i g_H|<=C ||H||_infinity/A.                    (2)

Here C is an absolute constant, independent of N, configuration and any minimum
activity fraction. A>=2 is enough. To prove the second inequality, expand

    Delta_i g_H=sum_j [Delta_j F_H(eta^i)-Delta_j F_H(eta)]. (3)

There are at most five j whose local exchange neighborhoods meet i. On these
terms the first-difference bound |Delta_j F_H|<=8||H||/A, together with
A(eta^i)>=A(eta)/2, bounds their total by C||H||/A.

For every other j, exchanges i,j commute and their local changes of A and A_H
are unaffected by the other exchange. Thus the corresponding term is a mixed
second difference of y/x, at x=A,y=A_H, in two directions (a,p),(b,q) with
|a|,|b|<=2 and |p|,|q|<=2||H||. If A>=8, every denominator in the interpolation
rectangle is at least A/2. Its second derivatives bound this difference by
C||H||/A^2. If 2<=A<8, all four actual configurations have activity at least
two; |F_H|<=||H|| bounds the difference by 4||H||, which is again at most
196||H||/A^2. Only originally active distant j contribute, at most A of them;
distant inactive j remain inactive after i. Summing proves (2).

This is precisely the extra locality information missing from a crude bounded
g_H estimate. It does not assert D(phi(A))=0 for nonlinear phi.

Put

    h_H=g_H/A.

Since |Delta_i A|<=2 and A(eta^i)>=A/2, (2) implies

    |h_H|<=C_H/A,  |Delta_i h_H|<=C_H/A^2,
    |L_native h_H|<=C_H/A.                               (4)

The last bound uses at most A active native events and bounded rates. None
of these estimates substitutes a typical activity of order N for a rare A.

## 3. Exact generator identity and superexponential control

Every native transition sends u to -u and the clean total native rate is cA.
Therefore

    L_native(u h_H)=-2c u A h_H-u L_native h_H,
    u g_H=-(1/(2c))L_native(u h_H)
                          -(1/(2c))u L_native h_H.       (5)

Apply the actual Dynkin martingale to u h_H. The endpoint divided by N^2 is
O(N^-2). Each native jump has size |h_H(eta^i)+h_H(eta)|<=C_H/A; its physical
bracket rate is at most C_H/A<=C_H/2. Hence the martingale divided by N^2 on
physical time N^2T is superexponentially negligible at speed N, by the bounded-
jump exponential inequality. The integral of the second term in (5) is bounded
by C_H int_0^T A^-1dt, already proved superexponentially negligible.

It follows that

    int_0^T u L_ex F_H(eta_(N^2t))dt
          is speed-N superexponentially negligible.       (6)

For smooth time-dependent H, h_H is linear in H at each configuration, with
the same bounds for its time derivative. Dynkin's added derivative term is
O(N^-2) after the current normalization. Uniform-in-terminal-time estimates
follow from maximal martingale bounds and inverse-activity domination.

The first weighted-current correction consequently holds at zero clock. All
these base-law superexponential statements transfer to bounded weak comparison
tilts by the same exact second-moment likelihood identity. The previously
reviewed spatial-tilt receiver, action topology, lower approximation and proof
of goodness therefore apply unchanged. The complete nonlocal action is (3) of
`NONLOCAL_ACTION_FROM_EVENT_MEMORY.md`, now also for gamma_N=0.

## 4. Compatibility with hidden phase amplitudes

Use the actual combined supplier
r_i=bar r_i[1+zeta_i cos(theta_i)] from
`HIDDEN_KINETICS_AND_DESIGNED_MEMORY.md`, with |zeta_i|<=b<1 and independent
phase diffusion kappa_N->infinity, but with NO external shared-bit clock.
Write R_tot=sum_i bar r_i zeta_i cos(theta_i). The actual total native rate is
cA+R_tot, and the exact replacement for (5) is

    u g_H=-(1/(2c))L_actual(u h_H)
           -(1/(2c))u L_actual h_H-(1/c)u R_tot h_H.      (7)

The phase generator acts trivially on u h_H and h_H. Bounded actual native
rates and (4) still give |L_actual h_H|<=C_H/A and a martingale bracket rate
at most C_H/A. The final term in (7) is phase-linear, with coefficients
u bar r_i zeta_i h_H bounded uniformly and independent of all actuated phases.
The established independent-phase Feynman--Kac estimate removes its accumulated
contribution at speed N. Use the valid bound sum_i||coefficient_i||_infinity^2
<=C_H N; no supremum/sum interchange is assumed.

Thus the same full programmed nonlocal action remains valid uniformly over
the stated arbitrary bounded hidden amplitudes, with only the supplied native
event updates and independent phase actuators. Initial arbitrary phases use
the same active warmup; actual initial association and full future laws remain
required. Hidden memory is neither copied nor reset.

## 5. Optional external resets and the complete slow-clock range

If 0<=gamma_N<=1, the generator identity (5) adds a remainder proportional to
gamma_N u h_H, which is bounded by C_H/A. Clock jumps of u h_H have bounded
bracket rate. The first corrector's clock occupation and martingale terms
remain negligible; for its bounded odd occupation term at very small gamma,
one can instead apply the same native identity to u F_H using h=F_H/A.
Its native remainder is O(1/A), while its amplitude and bracket remain bounded.
More explicitly, Delta_i(F_H/A)=O(A^-2), so this second application is identical
to (4)--(7), with gamma_N bounded. Therefore bounded nonnegative external rates,
including zero, require no inverse-gamma estimate.

For gamma_N>1 and gamma_N/N->0 the already reviewed positive-clock proof applies.
Splitting a sequence into these two regimes proves the same action for every
nonnegative gamma_N=o(N). This enlargement is an optional byproduct; zero clock
is the operationally useful new case.

## 6. What changed and what remains open

The mechanism no longer needs a continuous external shared-bit clock to recover
the desired full law. The bit is driven by the native events themselves. Its
update count remains order N^3 over the diffusive horizon in the warranted
interior regime; global coupling and atomic updates remain real resources.
The independent phase ports are still needed for the displayed unknown-kinetics
class, rather than inferred from the event bit alone.

Uniform ellipticity still uses fixed alpha<1 and b<1. The full spatial action
at alpha=1, or with unknown closed gates b=1, is not proved here. Exact bounded
current at alpha=1 remains valid under its separate transition-support premise.
The second-corrector argument does not imply a finite-N acquired confidence
bound, a joint apparatus-record LDP, or historical novelty of corrector methods.

# Inverse activity removes the weighted-current remainder

30 October 2026. Complementary constructive proof within Astra P1. The inverse-activity theorem below is proved at a uniformly elliptic reversible exclusion interface. Its application closes the weighted-corrector remainder for the shared-bit ring when `N gamma_N -> infinity` and `gamma_N/N -> 0`. It does **not** by itself prove the proposed nonlinear density/current large-deviation principle. In particular, the hydrodynamic receiver under the corrected spatial tilt remains a separate obligation.

The zero-external-clock version of the inverse-activity theorem is valid. The subsequent odd-in-the-bit corrector estimate uses an actual positive clock and does not establish the zero-clock weighted receiver.

## 1. A sufficiently general inverse-activity theorem

Let `eta` be an exclusion configuration on a periodic ring of `N` sites, with exactly `M_N` particles and `M_N/N -> m`, `0<m<1`. Write

\[
\delta_i=\eta_i-\eta_{i+1},\qquad a_i=\delta_i^2,
\qquad A(\eta)=\sum_i a_i.
\tag{1}
\]

Thus `A>=2` in every nontrivial particle sector. Work on physical time accelerated by `N^2`.

The complete finite-state process may contain an auxiliary state. Its reference law `mu_N` has uniform canonical visible marginal, and the full generator is reversible for `mu_N`. Each visible transition is a nearest-neighbor exchange, with physical rate between constants `q_*>0` and `q^*<infinity` on active bonds. The joint Dirichlet form dominates `q_* D_ex`, where the visible exchange form is evaluated at each fixed auxiliary state against the corresponding uniform visible conditional law. Auxiliary-only transitions do not change `eta`. Equivalently, it is enough to assume a product reference `mu_eta times mu_aux`, visible-only exchanges reversible in every fixed auxiliary state, and an additional reversible auxiliary generator. This last formulation directly covers the original `(eta,sigma)` shared-clock ring, including `gamma_N=0`.

Suppose the actual initial law satisfies

\[
\frac{d\nu_N}{d\mu_N}\le e^{hN+o(N)}
\tag{2}
\]

for one fixed finite `h`. On the finite ring, an arbitrary initial occupancy and one retained bit cost at most `2 binom(N,M_N)`, so (2) includes arbitrary initial laws in that sector. No initial flat spatial profile is needed.

**Theorem.** For every fixed `T<infinity` and `epsilon>0`,

\[
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb P_{\nu_N}
\left(\int_0^T\frac{dt}{A(\eta_{N^2t})}>\epsilon\right)
=-\infty.
\tag{3}
\]

The same conclusion holds under any mathematical native-rate tilt `r_i -> r_i exp(q_i)` with predictable `|q_i|<=K/N`, for fixed `K`, and unchanged auxiliary dynamics. This is a likelihood transfer, not a supplied control operation.

The proof does not assume that `A/N` is bounded below pointwise, or that rare paths resemble the canonical equilibrium. It combines three explicit conventional inputs and then gives the compactness argument joining them.

## 2. Density-path exponential tightness from reversibility

Let `pi_t^N=N^{-1} sum_i eta_i(N^2t) delta_(i/N)`. For a smooth periodic `G`, every native jump of `pi^N(G)` has magnitude at most `||G'||_infinity/N^2`, and its forward Dynkin martingale has predictable bracket over an interval of length `delta` at most

\[
q^*\|G'\|_\infty^2\delta/N.
\tag{4}
\]

The auxiliary jumps do not contribute. Under the stationary reversible law, the reversed process on `[0,T]` has the same generator. Subtracting its Dynkin martingale from the forward one cancels both generator integrals and gives the exact forward/backward identity

\[
\pi_t^N(G)-\pi_s^N(G)
=\tfrac12(M_t^G-M_s^G)
-\tfrac12(\widehat M_{T-s}^G-\widehat M_{T-t}^G).
\tag{5}
\]

The bounded-jump martingale exponential inequality, applied forward and backward on a finite interval grid, gives

\[
\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\limsup_N\frac1N\log
\mathbb P_{\mu_N}\left(
\sup_{|t-s|\le\delta}|\pi_t^N(G)-\pi_s^N(G)|>\epsilon
\right)=-\infty.
\tag{6}
\]

For example, at a fixed grid interval the exponent is bounded above by a constant times `-epsilon^2 N/(q^* ||G'||^2 delta+O(epsilon/N))`; the number of grid intervals is fixed before `N` grows. This is the elementary finite-chain instance of the classical Lyons–Zheng forward/backward method.

Interpolate each visible jump continuously between its neighboring states. The change in a weak density norm is deterministic `O(1/N)` (and `O_G(1/N^2)` on a fixed smooth test). Fourier truncation, the bound on total mass, and (6) give exponential tightness of these interpolated density paths in `C([0,T],H^{-3})`. All limits have densities `0<=rho<=1`, and conserved mass `m`. The usual countable-test diagonal construction supplies a compact set with any prescribed exponential escape cost. Multiplication by (2) transfers this assertion to the actual initializer. Irreducibility is unnecessary.

## 3. An exponential spatial energy estimate independent of the clock

Use the convention

\[
D_{\rm ex}(f)=\frac12\sum_i\int|f(\eta^i,z)-f(\eta,z)|^2d\mu_N.
\tag{7}
\]

For `||f||_2=1` and real coefficients `H_i`, invariance under each visible exchange gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|\left\langle\sum_iH_i\delta_i,f^2\right\rangle\right|
&=\frac12\left|\sum_iH_i\langle\delta_i(f^2-(f^i)^2)\rangle\right|\\
&\le\sqrt{2\sum_iH_i^2}\sqrt{D_{\rm ex}(f)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]

Complete the square against `q_* N^2 D_ex`. The top Feynman–Kac eigenvalue for the potential `N sum_i H_i delta_i` is at most `(2q_*)^{-1} sum_i H_i^2`. This holds separately for every time of a smooth time-dependent field; the usual `L2` norm differential inequality integrates the bound.

Define the continuous path functional

\[
\mathcal E_H(\rho)=\int_0^T\!\int\rho\,\partial_xH\,dxdt
-\frac1{2q_*}\int_0^T\!\int H^2\,dxdt.
\tag{9}
\]

Discrete summation by parts and Riemann sums have `O_H(1/N)` error before multiplication by `N`. Therefore, for each fixed smooth `H`,

\[
\limsup_N\frac1N\log
\mathbb P_{\nu_N}(\mathcal E_H(\pi^N)>R)\le h-R.
\tag{10}
\]

Here and below the same functional on the empirical path means its Riemann-sum version; its limit is (9). Its difference from the interpolated path version vanishes for each fixed field.

Take a countable dense set of smooth fields, including rational multiples. Functional duality gives

\[
\mathcal E(\rho):=\sup_H\mathcal E_H(\rho)
=\frac{q_*}{2}\int_0^T\!\int|\partial_x\rho|^2dxdt,
\tag{11}
\]

with value infinity if there is no square-integrable weak spatial derivative. No assertion that a single finite-`N` atomic path has a finite value of the continuum supremum is made. We use only finitely many tests at a time and then a compactness argument in Section 5. This avoids an unjustified interchange of an infinite supremum and an exponential expectation.

The general energy-estimate method is established. For a primary treatment of its role in exclusion large deviations, see Bertini–Landim–Mourragui, Section 3.2 and Lemma 3.3 of [Dynamical large deviations for the boundary driven weakly asymmetric exclusion process](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0804.2458). Equations (8)–(11) give the simpler periodic reversible estimate actually used here, without importing that paper's different generator or boundary conditions.

## 4. Occupation replacement forces small activity toward pure profiles

For a block of `ell` sites let `rho_ell(x)` be its average occupancy, and let `p_ell(x)` be its `ell-1` internal adjacent products divided by `ell`. Set

\[
U_\ell(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_x|p_\ell(x)-\rho_\ell(x)^2|.
\tag{12}
\]

The explicit variational one/two-block estimate proved in the accepted round7 file
`record_geometry/TILTED_HYDRODYNAMIC_RECEIVER.md`, equations (7)–(13), says

\[
\lim_{a\downarrow0}\limsup_N\frac1N
\sup_{\|f\|_2=1}
\{bN\langle U_{\lfloor aN\rfloor},f^2\rangle
-q_*N^2D_{\rm ex}(f)\}=0
\tag{13}
\]

for every fixed `b>0`. Apply it at each auxiliary state and integrate. Thus, for each `delta>0`,

\[
\lim_{a\downarrow0}\limsup_N\frac1N\log
\mathbb P_{\nu_N}\left(\int_0^T U_{\lfloor aN\rfloor}(\eta_{N^2t})dt>\delta\right)
=-\infty.
\tag{14}
\]

This use of the predecessor requires only its visible variational estimate and form domination, not an independently randomized local phase bath or a hydrodynamic identification. Although that file displays the Bernoulli reference, its conditional-block proof is unchanged at a fixed global particle count: all conditional block laws remain uniform canonical, and every intermediate permutation in the moving-particle estimate preserves the global canonical measure.

Let `chi(v)=v(1-v)` and define

\[
C_{N,\ell}(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_x\chi(\rho_\ell(x)).
\]

Averaging the internal pair products gives the deterministic inequality

\[
C_{N,\ell}(\eta)\le \frac{A(\eta)}{2N}+U_\ell(\eta)+\frac1\ell.
\tag{15}
\]

Indeed the average block density equals `m_N`, the average internal pair product is `(ell-1)/ell` times the global adjacent pair average, and `A/N=2m_N-2N^{-1}sum_i eta_i eta_(i+1)`.

At fixed `a>0`, the limiting functional is

\[
C_a(\rho)=\int\chi(B_a\rho)(x)dx,
\tag{16}
\]

where `B_a` is the periodic box average of width `a`. It is continuous in the weak measure topology on `0<=rho<=1`. In particular, its quadratic term is a double integral against the continuous triangular autocorrelation kernel of the box. Consequently it is continuous along the uniformly weakly converging compact density paths supplied in Section 2. As `a` decreases to zero, `C_a(rho_t)` converges to `int chi(rho_t)` in time `L1` by the approximation-of-identity theorem and boundedness.

## 5. The finite-test compactness proof of (3)

Suppose `int_0^T 1/A dt > epsilon`. Choose one fixed `K>2T/epsilon` and put `b_N(t)=1{A(eta_(N^2t))<=K}`. Since `A>=2`,

\[
\int_0^T\frac{dt}{A}\le T/K+\tfrac12\int_0^T b_N(t)dt.
\tag{17}
\]

Thus the bad event forces `int b_N > epsilon` after decreasing `epsilon` harmlessly if necessary.

Here is the deterministic exclusion of such bad paths from every finite-energy limit. Take a sequence of paths in a fixed compact density-path set, and assume:

1. each fixed test from the countable dense energy family eventually satisfies `E_H<=R`, for one finite `R`;
2. for scales `a_j down to 0` and tolerances `delta_j down to 0`, each fixed `j` eventually satisfies `int U_floor(a_j N) <= delta_j`;
3. the bad event in (17) holds.

Pass to a density-path limit `rho`, and to a weak-star subsequential limit `b` of the bounded functions `b_N` in `L infinity([0,T])`. Then `0<=b<=1` and `int b>=epsilon`. For each fixed `j`, multiply (15) by `b_N` and integrate. Its limit gives

\[
\int_0^T b(t)C_{a_j}(\rho_t)dt\le\delta_j.
\tag{18}
\]

Let `j` grow. The approximation-of-identity limit in Section 4 yields

\[
\int_0^T b(t)\!\int\chi(\rho_t(x))dxdt=0.
\tag{19}
\]

The energy conditions and (11) place `rho_t` in spatial `H^1` for almost every `t`. At each such time, `0<=rho_t<=1` and its integral is `m in (0,1)`. A function in `H^1` on the connected circle that is `{0,1}`-valued almost everywhere is constant: for example its absolutely continuous representative is continuous, or apply the Sobolev chain rule to `rho^2=rho`. Hence

\[
\int\chi(\rho_t)>0\quad\text{for almost every }t.
\tag{20}
\]

Equations (19) and (20) force `b=0` almost everywhere, a contradiction.

For completeness, the probabilistic quantifiers are finite at every stage. Fix any desired exponential cost `L`. Choose a compact density-path set with escape cost greater than `L` by Section 2, and choose `R>h+L+1`. Choose `a_j down to 0`, `delta_j down to 0` so that each replacement failure in (14) has limsup exponent below `-L-1`. If for every finite number of energy and replacement tests there existed arbitrarily large `N` and a bad path in the compact set passing those tests, a diagonal selection would produce exactly the contradictory sequence above. Therefore some finite number of tests excludes all such paths for sufficiently large `N`. A finite union bound, (10), and (14) bound the bad-event exponent by `-L`. Since `L` is arbitrary, (3) follows.

This proof pays for low-activity paths through their dynamical energy. It does not replace a speed-`N` rare event by its typical equilibrium concentration.

## 6. Bounded weak tilts and retained records

For a predictable native tilt `|q_i|<=K/N`, let `Z_q` be its path likelihood against the base process over physical time `N^2T`. The exact jump likelihood identity is

\[
Z_q^2=Z_{2q}\exp\left\{\int_0^{N^2T}\sum_i r_i(e^{q_i}-1)^2dv\right\}.
\tag{21}
\]

The total native rate is at most `q^* N`, so the extra exponent is at most `C_K N T`. The bounded likelihood exponential is a true martingale on the finite horizon, giving `E Z_q^2<=exp(C_KNT)`. Cauchy–Schwarz transfers every speed-`N` superexponential assertion above. No invariant measure of the tilted process is assumed.

Conditional-on-record use requires (2) at the chosen conditioning interface and the **complete future native and auxiliary conditional generator law**. A record revealing future native innovations invalidates this law even if the external clock itself is fresh. The theorem supplies neither initial preparation nor calibration confidence. Fixed calibration failure probability cannot be discarded in a rare-event claim.

## 7. Exact algebra for the ring weighted corrector

Now specialize to the round7 ring with even `N`,

\[
r_i=c(1+\alpha u\delta_i),\quad c=s/2,\quad
u=\sigma p(\eta),\quad 0\le\alpha<1,
\tag{22}
\]

where the external bit `sigma` flips at physical rate `gamma_N`. Native exchanges flip `p` and therefore `u`. The actual native rates in coordinates `(eta,sigma)` are uniformly elliptic and reversible at every fixed `sigma`, so (3) applies even if `gamma_N=0`.

Write

\[
L_{\rm ex}=\sum_i(T_i-I),\qquad
\mathcal D=\sum_i\delta_i(T_i-I),\qquad
L_{\rm native}=cL_{\rm ex}+c\alpha u\mathcal D.
\tag{23}
\]

For a smooth deterministic spatial field `H`, set `A_H=sum_i H_i a_i` and `F_H=A_H/A`. Then `|F_H|<=||H||_infinity`. A swap changes only its two neighboring activities, so `|Delta_i A|<=2`, `|Delta_i A_H|<=2||H||`, and `A(eta^i)>=A(eta)/2` on active edges. Thus

\[
|\Delta_i F_H|\le 8\|H\|_\infty/A,
\qquad |L_{\rm ex}F_H|\le8\|H\|_\infty.
\tag{24}
\]

There is an exact local-divergence identity for the asymmetric operator. Put

\[
q_j=\eta_j+2\eta_{j+1}+\eta_{j+2}
-2(\eta_j\eta_{j+1}+\eta_j\eta_{j+2}+\eta_{j+1}\eta_{j+2})
+4\eta_j\eta_{j+1}\eta_{j+2}.
\]

Its eight binary values lie in `[0,2]`, and direct expansion gives

\[
\mathcal D a_j=q_{j-1}-q_j,
\quad \mathcal D A=0,
\quad |\mathcal D A_H|\le2\sum_j|H_{j+1}-H_j|.
\tag{25}
\]

The identity `D A=0` is **not** extended to nonlinear functions of `A`. Instead, the exact quotient expansion is

\[
\mathcal D F_H
=\frac{\mathcal D A_H}{A}
-\sum_{i:\,a_i=1}\frac{\delta_i\Delta_i A
      (\Delta_i A_H-F_H\Delta_i A)}{A\,A(\eta^i)}.
\tag{26}
\]

Consequently

\[
|\mathcal D F_H|\le
\frac{2\sum_j|H_{j+1}-H_j|+16\|H\|_\infty}{A}
\le C_H/A.
\tag{27}
\]

For smooth `H(t,x)`, the constant is uniform on the fixed time interval.

It follows that

\[
uL_{\rm native}F_H=c\,uL_{\rm ex}F_H+c\alpha\mathcal D F_H
\tag{28}
\]

splits into a uniformly bounded odd-in-`sigma` term and a term dominated by `C_H/A`. The latter has superexponentially vanishing time integral by (3), including under every bounded weak comparison tilt in Section 6.

## 8. The odd term, clock term, and a larger allowed clock window

For a bounded visible function `v(eta)` and `V= sigma v`, the fair-sign integration-by-parts inequality is

\[
|\langle V,f^2\rangle|\le\sqrt2\|v\|_\infty
\sqrt{D_\sigma(f)},\qquad \|f\|_2=1,
\]

where `D_sigma=(1/2) int(f(eta,-sigma)-f(eta,sigma))^2`. Against the macroscopic clock form `N^2 gamma_N D_sigma`, Feynman–Kac gives

\[
\log\mathbb E_{\mu_N}\exp\left(bN\int_0^T V_tdt\right)
\le b^2T\|v\|_\infty^2/(2\gamma_N).
\tag{29}
\]

Apply this to `u L_ex F_H=sigma[p L_ex F_H]` using (24). It is superexponentially negligible at speed `N` provided `N gamma_N -> infinity`. Apply it to `gamma_N u F_H`; its divided log-moment cost is `O(gamma_N/N)`. The associated compensated clock sum has the same divided log-moment cost. Therefore both are negligible if

\[
N\gamma_N\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad \gamma_N/N\longrightarrow0.
\tag{30}
\]

The round7 hypothesis `gamma_N -> infinity`, `gamma_N/N -> 0` is a sufficient subcase. A fixed strictly positive clock, or a slowly vanishing clock satisfying the left condition, also suffices for this remainder estimate. No claim is made at `gamma_N=0` using (29).

Here is the complete path identity behind the receiving statement. Let

\[
K_H(t)=\sum_{\text{native events}\le t}
[H_i\delta_i-\alpha u_-F_H(\eta_-)]
-\int_0^t cS_H(\eta_v)dv,
\quad S_H=\sum_iH_i\delta_i.
\tag{31}
\]

The increment field is evaluated at the event's macroscopic time for time-dependent `H`. The total native rate is `cA`, and the two unwanted drifts cancel, so `K_H` is exactly a martingale. Applying the jump rule to `uF_H` gives, for time-independent `H`,

\[
\begin{aligned}
J_H(t)-K_H(t)-\int_0^t cS_Hdv
={}&\frac\alpha2[u_0F_H(\eta_0)-u_tF_H(\eta_t)]\\
&-\frac\alpha2 L_H(t)
-\frac\alpha2\int_0^t uL_{\rm native}F_Hdv\\
&-\alpha C_H^{\rm clock}(t)
-\alpha\gamma_N\int_0^t uF_Hdv,
\end{aligned}
\tag{32}
\]

where `L_H` is the compensated native sum of `u_- Delta_i F_H`, and `C_H^clock` is the compensated clock sum of `u_- F_H`. For smooth time-dependent `H`, add the deterministic time-derivative integral `alpha/(2N^2) int u partial_t F_H dv` to the right; after division by `N^2` it is `O(N^-2)`.

The native martingale `L_H` has bounded jumps and physical bracket rate at most `C_H/A<=C_H/2`, by (24). Its normalized accumulated contribution on time `N^2T`, divided by `N^2`, is superexponentially negligible at speed `N` by its bounded-jump exponential inequality. The boundary is `O(N^-2)`. Equations (3), (28)–(30) handle every remaining term. These estimates hold uniformly over terminal times: deterministic integral domination handles (27), while finite time grids or maximal martingale inequalities handle the bounded odd sources and martingales.

Thus the actual weighted current has the proved replacement

\[
\frac{J_H(N^2t)}{N^2}
\;\simeq_{\rm superexp,\,N}\;
\frac{K_H(N^2t)}{N^2}
+c\int_0^tS_H(\eta_{N^2v})dv
\tag{33}
\]

on every fixed horizon, under (30) and under all the bounded weak comparison tilts specified above. This removes the exact remainder identified in the round7 attack file. The martingale bracket there remains exact; the new work is the justified passage back to the **actual** current.

## 9. An actual unforced hydrodynamic consequence

Suppose, additionally, that the initial empirical density converges in probability to an actual profile `rho_0(x) dx`, with `0<=rho_0<=1` and interior total mass. It may be deterministic or random at the microscopic level, subject to (2). Under (22) and (30), the actual empirical density and spatial current converge on every fixed horizon to

\[
\partial_t\rho=c\partial_x^2\rho,\qquad \rho(0)=\rho_0,
\qquad j=-c\partial_x\rho.
\tag{34}
\]

To verify this corollary, apply (33) to `H_i=N(G_(i+1)-G_i)`. This family has uniformly bounded sup norm and discrete variation for each fixed smooth `G`. Exact continuity identifies the left side with the change in `pi^N(G)`, and the drift is `c pi^N(Delta_N G)`. The martingale in (31), divided by `N^2`, has bracket `O(1/N)` because its native jumps and rates are bounded. Hence every exponentially tight density subsequential limit satisfies the weak heat equation. Its bounded weak solution is unique.

# Known-center Phase I for the bounded-witness discovery SDP

This closes a complexity-interface correction to `EFFECTIVE_PORT.md`.
The bounded-witness premise supplies existence of a strict certificate,
but does NOT supply that feasible center. Therefore the known-center
Turing theorem is NOT invoked directly on the original discovery SDP.
The following ordinary Phase I construction acquires its actual premise.

Controlling primary: de Klerk–Vallentin1507.03549v2, Theorem1.1 (attributed
there to Grötschel–Lovász–Schrijver). Its input includes a KNOWN rational
feasible matrix X0 and known inner/outer Frobenius radii in the equality
affine space. It returns a rational feasible point at any positive
requested objective accuracy in polynomial time in the SDP size, data
bits and logarithmic radius/accuracy parameters. Here every such input
is constructed for a Phase I problem, not assumed for the discovery set.

## 1. Known equality point

Use the degree/boxes of `EFFECTIVE_PORT.md`: k=(D-3)/2, d=k+2,
N=ell-d, n_G=6*binom(ell+3,3), A=A_P, Gamma=3B64^ell.
Let x list all homogeneous P coefficients, nu and upper-triangular Q
entries. The exact coefficient equations have rational form Ex=f.
The desired inequalities are

    Q-(m/8)D_ell >=0,
    b_i+x_i>=0, b_i-x_i>=0 for every coordinate i,

where b_i is2A for primitive coefficients,2Gamma for Gram entries,
and Lambda+2 for nu. These coordinate boxes also bound all possible
unknown normalizers; nothing is supplied by an optimizer.

There is an explicit rational equality point x0: set P=0 and nu=0, then
represent the known polynomial

    T^(N+k+1) D_0 F

by a symmetric Gram Q0 in the full basis A^alpha h_j, |alpha|=ell.
Every monomial of A-degree2ell and h-degree2 splits into two such basis
monomials. Assign its coefficient to a diagonal Gram entry, or equally to
the two symmetric off-diagonal entries. This is the same elementary exact
coefficient operation used in the original certificate qualifier. Q0 may
be indefinite; it is NOT mislabelled a feasible point. Acquisition is
finite rational monomial arithmetic, polynomial in the finite map/output
size. No alpha, min-eigenvalue, gap or convex feasibility oracle is needed.

## 2. Artificial slack with a KNOWN strict center

Introduce one real scalar t and replace all desired inequalities by

    S(x,t)=Q-(m/8)D_ell+t I >=0,
    b_i+x_i+t>=0, b_i-x_i+t>=0,
    T0+t>=0, T0-t>=0.                              (P1)

The same exact equalities Ex=f remain. Define computable rational numbers

    R_G=max_j sum_l |(Q0-(m/8)D_ell)_(jl)|,
    R_box=max_i max(0,|x0_i|-b_i),
    t0=2+R_G+R_box, T0=2t0+2.                      (P2)

At (x0,t0), Gershgorin gives S>=2I. Every scalar block in(P1) is>=2.
Thus the block-diagonal matrix

    X0=diag(S(x0,t0), {b_i+x0_i+t0,b_i-x0_i+t0}_i,
            T0+t0,T0-t0)

is an EXPLICIT rational positive-definite feasible matrix, with X0>=2I.
It is acquired without knowing the original bounded witness.

## 3. Standard SDP form and radii

Let n_x be the length of x and n_S=n_G+2n_x+2. The affine image

    X(x,t)=diag(S(x,t),{b_i+x_i+t,b_i-x_i+t}_i,T0+t,T0-t)

subject to Ex=f is a rational affine subspace of symmetric n_S matrices.
It is specified by exact rational linear equations: off-block entries are
zero and the displayed blocks have their affine relations. The map is
injective, since the difference of each paired scalar block recovers2x_i
and the last pair recovers2t. Its image/range equations can be computed by
exact rational elimination in polynomial bit cost. The objective t is a
fixed linear trace functional of the last two scalar blocks.

The intersection of this affine image with X>=0 is exactly(P1). The known
X0 has a Frobenius inner ball of radius r0=1/2 in this affine space because
its smallest eigenvalue is>=2; no unknown-center theorem is used here.

For a known outer radius, put bmax=max_i b_i and

    C0=2bmax+2T0+(m/8)4^ell+1.

For EVERY Phase I feasible point, |t|<=T0, and the paired scalar
inequalities imply |x_i|<=b_i+T0. Each matrix entry of X is bounded byC0:
the diagonal of S additionally pays(m/8)D_ell, whose entries are<=
(m/8)4^ell. Hence ||X||F<=n_S C0. X0 is feasible as well, so the known
outer radius about X0 can be chosen

    R0=2n_S C0+1.                                  (P3)

All numbers have polynomial bit size in the finite map size/ell and the
given rational data. In particular no logarithm of an unknown center's
distance appears in(P2),(P3).

## 4. A known accuracy forces a usable certificate

The bounded-witness construction, whose center is unknown, proves there
EXISTS x* with

    Q* >=(m/4)D_ell,
    |P*_coefficient|<=A, |Q*ij|<=Gamma,
    |nu*|<=Lambda+1.

Set the known positive rational

    s=min(m/16,A/2,Gamma/2,1/2).                    (P4)

Then (x*,-s) is Phase I feasible: its PSD slack is at least(m/16)I;
the doubled boxes retain positive slack, and |s|<=1/2<T0. Therefore
the optimum of min t over(P1) is at most-s.

Now apply the PRIMARY known-center theorem to THIS Phase I SDP, with its
acquired X0,r0,R0 and objective accuracy s/2. It returns an exact rational
Phase I feasible matrix with t<=-s/2<0. Recover its rational x by the
paired-block differences. Then

    Q-(m/8)D_ell >= -t I >0,

and the original, unrelaxed boxes hold. The coefficient equalities are
exact as part of the rational affine image. Consequently a valid strict
rational angular certificate has actually been acquired. Final coefficient
identity/PSD verification is still performed; a particular floating solver
is not the algorithm guaranteed by this complexity theorem.

The weighted floor gives a direct full-domain strong Jensen margin
m/[576(1+|nu_out|)] by the already paid bound
|D_nu |A|^4|<=24(1+|nu|)T|h|² and quartic Bregman inequality. No largest
multinomial factor in ell is lost.

There is also a sound finite FAILURE interpretation. On an arbitrary input,
if the exact near-optimal feasible output has t_out>=0, the theorem's
objective guarantee implies val>=t_out-s/2>=-s/2>-s. This rigorously excludes
EVERY witness satisfying the DECLARED eta,W,Lambda bounds, because such a
witness would force val<=-s. Thus the operation always returns either an
actual QC certificate or a qualified rejection of that bounded witness
contract. A successful certificate need not itself have C2 norm<=W, so
this is not exact membership decision of the bounded class. Rejection
does not refute QC, a weaker-margin or larger-norm witness, or the entire
unbounded heat-form class. No unqualified finite-SDP-failure inference is
made.

## 5. Cost and scope

This gives a polynomial Turing acquisition guarantee in the finite Phase I
size/data bits and log(R0/r0),log(1/s), under the explicit bounded-witness
promise of `EFFECTIVE_PORT.md`. The dimensions there are polynomial in the
NUMERICAL W,eta^-1,Lambda,H_F at fixed physical dimension, with a very
large exponent. This is not a practical generic runtime, a bit-polynomial
bound in those magnitudes, a bound obtained from F alone, or QC-completeness.

Phase I and the known-center complexity theorem are established ordinary
tools; no generic optimization novelty is claimed. The acquired operation
is the full bound-and-search composition for this smooth heat-form class,
including the center that a direct invocation would have left unpaid.
No source/optimizer fixture or new physical operation was run here. The
generic Phase I/Turing solver is specified and proved, not implemented
end-to-end; actual finite execution remains the separate frozen input
certificate and its independent exact consumers.

1. New result: how probe retention changes stationary-state learning

Let the unknown, fixed, memoryless  $d$ -dimensional channel satisfy $J_{\mathcal E}\succeq \nu I_{d^2}/d^2.$ 

The task is to return a classical density-matrix estimate  $\widehat\rho$  of its unique stationary state, with $\|\widehat\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}\|_1\le\epsilon$ 

with probability at least  $2/3$ .

Acquisition uses fresh blocks. Within a block, a prepared probe passes through  $\mathcal E$  at most  $B$  consecutive times, then is measured or discarded. Classical choices may adapt between blocks. A fresh reference is allowed within a block for the lower bound. There are no intermediate controls or measurements, and no quantum memory carried between blocks.

For fixed  $d$ ,  $0<\nu\le1/20$ , and sufficiently small  $\epsilon$ , the derived minimax law is $\boxed{
N_{\mathrm{opt}}
=
\Theta_d\!\left(
\frac{1}
{\nu^2\min\{B,\nu^{-1}\}\epsilon^2}
\right).
}$ 

Here  $N_{\mathrm{opt}}$  is worst-case expected source calls. The upper construction has a deterministic acquisition budget.

 | Maximum retained block | Source-call scaling

 | Measure after every call,  $B=1$  |  $\Theta_d(\nu^{-2}\epsilon^{-2})$

The Choi promise gives the mathematical decomposition $\mathcal E=\nu\mathcal D+(1-\nu)\mathcal F,

For fixed dimension, this needs  $O_d(\eta^{-2})$  block observations at constant confidence.

There is a direct classical reconstruction that avoids assuming the fitted map is physical. Make the linear fit Hermiticity preserving and trace preserving. On traceless Hermitian matrices, it contracts by at most  $1-\gamma_b+\eta$ . Its trace-one affine fixed point  $\sigma$  therefore satisfies $\|\sigma-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}\|_1
\le \frac{\eta}{\gamma_b-\eta}.$ 

Clip negative eigenvalues and renormalize. This increases the error by at most another copy of that bound: $\|\widehat\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}\|_1
\le \frac{2\eta}{\gamma_b-\eta}.$ 

Taking  $\eta=\epsilon\gamma_b/4$  is sufficient for  $\epsilon\le1$ . Consequently, $N=O_d\!\left(\frac{b}{\epsilon^2\gamma_b^2}\right),$ 

which gives the displayed law.

The enabling interface is concrete: known input preparations, ordinary output measurements, one retained  $d$ -level probe, a fixed-size tomography table, a linear solve on  $d^2-1$  coordinates, and a  $d\times d$  spectral projection. No source adjoint, inverse, labelled reset, shifted control, or channel-synthesis catalogue is required. Preparation, readout, arithmetic precision and holding time remain real costs.

Matching lower bound

The complementary review found a slow coherent family that penalizes immediate measurement. I extended it to the full-rank Choi-floor class.

Let  $X_2,Y_2,Z_2$  act on a two-dimensional subspace and vanish outside it. Set $s=2\nu,\qquad
\tau=\frac{I+\tfrac12 Z_2}{d},$ 

and consider $\mathcal E_u
=
\operatorname{Ad}_{e^{-isuY_2/2}}
\circ
\left[(1-s)\operatorname{Id}+s\mathcal R_\tau\right],
\qquad u\in[0.8,1.2].$ 

Its normalized Choi matrix has floor at least  $\nu I/d^2$ . Writing  $p=1-s$ , its stationary  $Z_2$  expectation is $f_s(u)=
\frac1d
\frac{s[\cos(su)-p]}
{1-2p\cos(su)+p^2},$ 

with  $|f_s'(u)|\ge1/(4d)$  throughout the stated range.

For a block of length  $b$ , strengthen the experimenter by revealing the last-reset branch at the end of the block. The surviving rotation length has the law $L=\min\{\operatorname{Geom}(s),b\},
\qquad
s^2\mathbb E L^2\le\min\{s^2b^2,2\}.$ 

For two nearby parameters separated by  $\Delta u$ , a bounded-generator purification argument gives block root fidelity at least $1-\frac{\Delta u^2}{8}\min\{s^2b^2,2\}.$ 

This remains valid with a fresh reference. Summing the resulting distinguishability budget across blocks bounds information per source call by a constant times $\Delta u^2\,s\min\{sB,1\}.$ 

Two parameters separated by order  $d\epsilon$  have stationary expectations separated by more than  $2\epsilon$ . Distinguishing them yields the matching lower bound. The internal review also checked the decision-tree extension to adaptive block lengths and worst-case expected cost.

This result is internally reviewed, not externally accepted or priority established. Optimizing coherent interrogation time under noise has substantial metrology predecessors; those precedents prevent presenting probe retention itself as a new idea. The specific result developed here is the stationary-state learning law, its Choi-floor lower family, and the fully charged block-tomography construction. arxiv.org+1
